entries.title: Restore dense and sparse feature-hashing matrices
entries.head: 6b37a2956513d48c48d1dd4cf7b372b8dcc46193
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Both documented output modes of FeatureHasher fail before producing a feature matrix. The dense path passes the feature dimension as the dtype argument to np.zeros. The sparse path hands SciPy a one-shot zip object for coordinates; ordinary nonempty inputs and empty inputs raise a coordinate-count error.

## Change

Allocate the dense output with its two-dimensional shape. Build explicit row and column lists for the sparse output. Keep the existing hash mapping, values and collision accumulation.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest numpy_ml/tests/test_feature_hasher.py -q`: 14 passed. All 14 cases fail on unchanged master b0359af.

The tests use fixed MD5 bucket expectations and cover dense/CSR output, dict and list inputs, byte and tuple feature keys, collisions, negative and fractional values, empty rows and an empty collection. Native package imports on Python 3.9.25, NumPy 1.26.4 and SciPy 1.13.1. Black checks on the changed source region and new tests, plus git diff --check, pass.

The full repository suite was not rerun for this isolated matrix-construction change.

entries.title: Expose invertible fitted standardization statistics
entries.head: 2f407f2ca6affd64d387bb0da27cb4ad8f87a1da
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Standardizer.parameters tests for mean/std attributes, but fit stores _mean/_std. A fitted instance therefore reports both statistics as None and inverse_transform fails with TypeError. Zero-variance training features also retain a zero scale and produce nonfinite transformed values.

## Change

Expose the fitted attributes through parameters, and use unit scale for zero-variance features. This preserves finite forward transforms and permits reconstruction of the original values, including held-out data whose previously constant feature changes.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest numpy_ml/tests/test_standardizer_statistics.py numpy_ml/tests/test_preprocessing.py::test_standardizer -q`: 10 passed.

The nine new cases give eight failures and one passing control on unchanged master b0359af. They cover all four centering/scaling configurations, ordinary and constant columns, stored statistics, training and held-out data, inverse reconstruction and an unfitted control. Forward results are compared with sklearn StandardScaler.

Native Python 3.9.25, NumPy 1.26.4 and scikit-learn 1.6.1. Black checks on the modified source region and new tests, plus git diff --check, pass. The full repository suite was not rerun.

entries.title: Apply punctuation filtering before whitespace-token stopword removal
entries.head: 3515629ef93cb162051362a668518767cb3674d8
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`tokenize_whitespace` computes punctuation-stripped values into `line` but returns the original `words`. The default filtering therefore leaves punctuation attached to vocabulary entries and prevents punctuation-bearing stop words from being removed. Punctuation-only strings also become vocabulary entries.

## Change
Write stripped, nonempty tokens back to `words` before applying stop-word filtering. Keep the existing lowercase and filtering switches. Add direct flag-combination tests and end-to-end Vocabulary and TFIDF checks.

## Validation
- The 11 new tests against unchanged upstream: 7 failed, 4 passed.
- The new tests plus the existing TFIDF test: 12 passed on Python 3.9.25 with native package imports.
- Independent read-only review covered the filtering semantics and downstream tests.
- The broader existing preprocessing suite has known Librosa 0.11 reference-call incompatibilities (three tests call keyword-only APIs positionally); this patch does not change those tests.

entries.title: Match Fourier coefficients and odd-length frequency bins to the DFT convention
entries.head: 36f0ec429fc5ef3ebe9b798f260e0273720ff669
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`DFT` builds the documented negative-exponent Fourier basis but evaluates it with `np.vdot`, which conjugates that basis. This reverses complex phase and gives incorrect coefficients for complex-valued inputs. `dft_bins(..., positive_only=True)` also places the final frequency at Nyquist for odd-length frames, even though their last DFT bin is below Nyquist.

## Change
Evaluate the existing Fourier basis with matrix multiplication, and generate positive frequencies as `k * fs / N`. These changes make coefficient values and their frequency coordinates follow the same DFT convention. Existing real-signal magnitude and power behavior remains covered.

## Validation
- The 35 new tests against unchanged upstream: 17 failed, 18 passed.
- New tests plus the existing DFT test: 36 passed on Python 3.9.25.
- References include NumPy FFT/frequency helpers, a hard-coded four-point sine phase, real/complex inputs, odd/even/singleton lengths, and magnitude/power controls.
- Independent read-only review found no blockers.
- Existing full preprocessing tests have three unrelated Librosa 0.11 reference-call incompatibilities; the new frequency tests use NumPy rather than those incompatible calls.

entries.title: Preserve special-token frequencies during TF-IDF reindexing
entries.head: d68a1e34e891fa2787bd090b5856d210efc83264
entries.published_body:
## Problem

TFIDFEncoder._sort_tokens reindexes ordinary term frequencies but discards the frequencies of <bol>, <eol> and <unk>. Explicitly requesting those columns returns zeros instead of their TF-IDF values. An empty document or a document filtered entirely into <unk> can also fail during transform because its term-frequency mapping has become empty.

## Change

Copy each special token's existing document counts to its new column index, as already done for ordinary terms. Preserve ordinary-first alphabetical ordering and the public option to omit special columns.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest numpy_ml/tests/test_tfidf_special_counts.py numpy_ml/tests/test_preprocessing.py::test_tfidf -q`: 11 passed.

All ten new cases fail on unchanged master b0359af. Handwritten term counts and independently calculated TF-IDF expectations cover smoothing on/off, normal and multiline documents, vocabulary filtering, minimum-frequency filtering, and empty documents. Assertions cover both complete and ordinary-only outputs plus the reindexed per-document counts.

Native Python 3.9.25 and NumPy 1.26.4. Black checks on the modified source region and complete new tests, plus git diff --check, pass. The full repository suite was not rerun.

entries.title: Preserve signal strides when constructing zero-copy frames
entries.head: 46bf4c1a909aea096c68675f977e1ea7b24dcd1e
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`to_frames` derives both output strides from `x.itemsize`, assuming contiguous input. For a subsampled or reversed signal view, the resulting frames read different samples from the requested logical signal and can point outside that view.

## Change
Use the input's actual one-dimensional sample stride for both frame and hop strides. The returned frames remain zero-copy views, with the existing writeability behavior.

## Validation
- The 12 new tests against unchanged upstream: 8 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus the existing framing test: 13 passed on Python 3.9.25.
- Slicing-based expected windows cover contiguous, subsampled and reversed views, two hop sizes, both writeability settings, shared storage and mutation aliasing.
- The reversed-input fixture is placed inside a larger owned buffer, so the old implementation can be tested without reading outside the allocation.
- Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Replace learned byte-pair codebooks deterministically on refit
entries.head: 4108dc68f468b356d2e21ce183286115a29cf4c7
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Fitting a BytePairEncoder again overwrites token IDs without removing the old byte-to-token entries. After learning ab and then xy, encoding and decoding abab can silently return xyxy. Learned token IDs also inherit the iteration order of a set, so identical training data can produce different codebooks under different Python hash seeds.

## Change

After the new vocabulary has been learned, replace both maps with the base 256-byte alphabet and add the current learned tokens in a stable order. This keeps the two maps consistent and makes successful refits replace the previous codebook. The existing merge budget and merge-selection algorithm remain unchanged.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest numpy_ml/tests/test_bpe_codebook_refit.py numpy_ml/tests/test_preprocessing.py::test_huffman numpy_ml/tests/test_preprocessing.py::test_tfidf -q`: 5 passed.

All three new regression cases fail on unchanged master b0359af. They cover refitting with zero and one permitted merge, comparison with a fresh encoder, exact round-trips for old/new/unseen Unicode text, and native subprocesses with PYTHONHASHSEED values 1, 7 and 11.

Python 3.9.25 and NumPy 1.26.4, normal package imports. Black checks on the changed source region and new test file, plus git diff --check, pass. Full repository tests and large-corpus timing were not run.

entries.title: Preserve complete UTF-8 bytes when splitting punctuation
entries.head: 22254636cc6427b15353d8a12107c4b293a13433
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`tokenize_bytes_raw(..., splitter="punctuation")` applies its punctuation regex to decimal byte values without numeric boundaries. ASCII punctuation codes can match inside unrelated UTF-8 bytes: `95` is matched inside `195` and `40` inside `240`. Splitting text such as `café!` or `🙂?` therefore corrupts the original bytes.

## Change
Require a complete decimal byte before treating it as punctuation. Preserve the existing capture group, ASCII punctuation splitting and empty-piece behavior.

## Validation
- The 13 new tests against unchanged upstream: 4 failed, 9 passed.
- New tests plus the existing Huffman test: 14 passed on Python 3.9.25 with native package imports.
- UTF-8 byte reconstruction and decoding cover accented Latin, Greek and emoji input; a hard-coded byte-group example verifies the actual split boundaries. ASCII, decimal text, empty text and `splitter=None` are controls.
- Black and `git diff --check` passed; independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: fix(mutual): rank choices by loglikelihood for all retrieval metrics
entries.head: 51442935faabf33ec15fc2cb8bb2020fb863fe48
entries.published_body:
## Problem

MuTual receives `(loglikelihood, is_greedy)` pairs from the multiple-choice task. Its current `np.argmax(results)` flattens both fields, so greedy flags can determine the reported top-1 choice. The other metrics sort entire tuples, allowing those flags to break likelihood ties. As a concrete example, results `[(-4, False), (-3, False), (-1, False), (-2, False)]` with gold answer C currently report `r@1=0`, `r@2=0`, and `mrr=1`.

## Change

Rank choice indices using only the loglikelihood field, then derive all three metrics from the gold choice's single rank. Equal loglikelihoods retain choice order. Update the task version to 2.1 and document the scoring correction; `mutual_plus` inherits the same configuration and implementation.

## Validation

- Four gold positions with two greedy-flag patterns verify the actual ranking metrics.
- Equal-likelihood cases verify that greedy flags cannot alter tie handling and that all metrics agree on one rank.
- Both real task YAML files are loaded into a native `ConfigurableTask` using an in-memory dataset. The tests construct four loglikelihood requests and verify the callback's metrics without downloading data or models.
- Baseline: 7 failures and 7 passing controls with the final regression cases.
- Fixed: all 14 new cases and 8 existing metric tests pass (22 total).
- Ruff 0.16.3 checks and formatting, plus `git diff --check`, pass.

No full-model benchmark or complete repository suite was run. This corrects metric computation and changes scores affected by the bug; it does not claim that model quality itself improved.

entries.title: Fix IFEval filtering of zero-valued instruction arguments
entries.head: 6df6cb37f4babcc3b68bb79d71a711ef2cc26e88
entries.published_body:
## Summary

IFEval currently removes every falsy instruction argument before constructing a checker. Zero is a valid value for constraints such as the number of placeholders, bullet points, or highlighted sections. Removing it causes the checker to sample a new requirement, so a response satisfying the recorded zero constraint can be scored incorrectly.

Keep all non-None arguments in strict and loose evaluation. Apply the same correction to the standard, leaderboard, and multilingual implementations, and advance their task metadata versions. The original Google evaluation code also passes the recorded argument values through to the instruction constructor.

## Validation

- New regression tests against the upstream base: 14 failed, 12 passed, 26 skipped.
- With this change, the new tests plus the existing metrics tests: 34 passed, 26 skipped.
- The executed tests use the real placeholder, bullet-point, and highlight checkers, nonzero and empty-response controls, and ConfigurableTask integration with the standard and leaderboard YAML configurations.
- Ruff 0.16.3 lint and formatting checks, and git diff --check pass. Existing typing annotations in the two touched English utility files are updated to satisfy that Ruff configuration.

The 26 Spanish/Catalan cases are skipped because the required spaCy language models are not installed. NLTK's downloader rejected the proxied Punkt resource download in this environment; the executed regular-expression checkers do not need that corpus. A full benchmark run and tokenizer-dependent instruction tests were not run.

This corrects interpretation of recorded task constraints; it does not claim an improvement in model capability.

entries.title: fix(mmmu): prevent numeric fragments from receiving answer credit
entries.head: cc1c96637d212286164bb287f2a135755d1d464f
entries.published_body:
## Problem

MMMU's numeric extractor independently scans comma-separated, scientific, and ordinary numbers, then concatenates the matches. The same numeric span can therefore contribute several different answer candidates. For example, `The answer is 1.25e3.` contributes 1250, 1, and 3 after normalization, so a question whose correct answer is 3 incorrectly receives acc=1. Likewise, `1,234.5` contributes false 1234 and 234.5 candidates. Leading-dot scientific notation can also be read without its decimal point.

## Change

Run the patterns together in one non-overlapping scan, prioritizing complete comma-separated and scientific forms. Keep the existing numeric rounding, string-answer handling, and multiple-choice logic. Two pre-existing whole-file Ruff findings are also resolved without changing behavior: explicit `zip(..., strict=False)` and an equivalent combined conditional.

The current [original MMMU parser](https://github.com/MMMU-Benchmark/MMMU/blob/main/mmmu/utils/eval_utils.py) has the same overlapping extraction. This is a correction to that behavior, not a claim of exact parser equivalence. Task and group metadata move from 0.0 to 0.1, and the README explicitly identifies the difference and keeps the historical model scores labeled as version 0.0. Results affected by these formats should not be directly compared across parser versions.

## Validation

- 27 new tests on the upstream base: 15 failed, 12 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing core metrics tests: 35 passed.
- Cases cover complete numeric extraction, false-fragment rejection in process_results, genuine numeric answers, multiple independently stated numbers, and multiple-choice controls.
- Native ConfigurableTask instances loaded from the actual MMMU math YAML construct generation requests and score the responses using an in-memory Dataset.
- All eight task/group metadata files parse at version 0.1.
- Pinned Ruff 0.16.3 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

No model inference, images, external benchmark download, or full repository suite was run. This corrects answer scoring; it does not demonstrate any improvement in a model's capability.

entries.title: fix(chartqa): compare explicit percentages in the same units
entries.head: 741ab752f49c6397f6e762c3b456ed476aae49c5
entries.published_body:
## Problem

ChartQA's relaxed scorer attempts a one-sided division by 100 whenever either value contains `%`, including when both values explicitly use percentages. Consequently, `1%` and `100%`, or `0.5%` and `50%`, can incorrectly receive full credit despite differing by a factor of 100. This also affects the explicit-final-answer path of the anywhere scorer.

## Change

Apply the existing unit-conversion fallback only when exactly one value contains `%`. Values that both use percentages are compared in the same units using the existing 5% relative tolerance. The historical permissive conversion when only one value contains `%` remains unchanged. Equivalent conditional and generator-expression cleanups address existing whole-file Ruff findings without changing the non-final-answer fallback.

The adapted [Mistral reference scorer](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-evals/blob/main/eval/metrics.py) contains the same behavior. This correction is therefore recorded as task version 0.1, inherited by chartqa, chartqa_llama, and chartqa_llama_90. The README identifies the scoring difference: affected relaxed/anywhere scores should not be directly compared with version 0.0; exact-match scoring is unchanged.

## Validation

- 59 new tests on the upstream base: 22 failed, 37 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing core metrics tests: 67 passed.
- Controls cover reversed and negative factor-of-100 errors, zeros, the relative-tolerance boundary, one-sided percentage conversions, ordinary numeric answers, multiple references, and the original anywhere fallback.
- Native ConfigurableTask instances loaded from all three actual YAML configurations construct generation requests and score in-memory Dataset examples.
- All three resolved configurations report version 0.1.
- Pinned Ruff 0.16.3 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

No model inference, chart images, external benchmark download, or full repository suite was run. The tests establish scoring correctness for these cases, not a change in model capability.

entries.title: Avoid squared-deviation overflow in metric uncertainty
entries.head: 2d1098d34c58e469e32936525a1f9e8cec7dd25e
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Population and sample standard deviation square every centered observation before taking a square root. The intermediate square can overflow or underflow even when the resulting standard deviation is representable. For example, values scaled by `1e200` raise `OverflowError`, while values scaled by `1e-200` incorrectly produce zero uncertainty.

This also interrupts real bootstrap aggregation: normalized finite log probabilities with a mean loss near 400 produce representable perplexities, but computing their bootstrap standard error overflows during squaring.

## Change

Use `math.hypot` to compute the centered-deviation norm, then divide by the square root of the population or sample denominator. Share that calculation between the two standard-deviation functions. Retain the existing calculation when the mean is non-finite, preserving NaN/infinity behavior and insufficient-sample errors.

This fixes intermediate squared-deviation range errors. It does not address overflow in the existing mean accumulation or an unscaled deviation norm that itself exceeds the floating-point range.

## Validation

- Original source: **9 failed, 15 passed** in the 24 new regression/control cases.
- Patched source plus the complete existing `tests/test_metrics.py`: **32 passed**.
- A 100-digit Decimal variance/square-root reference covers population and sample deviations at scales from `1e-200` to `1e200`, with exact zero absolute tolerance for small results.
- Native `ConfigurableTask` processing and evaluator aggregation cover 32 bootstrap replicates of ordinary and large finite perplexities. A separately reproduced resampling sequence and Decimal standard deviation provide the reference; no model inference was run.
- Controls cover constant data, non-finite observations, unchanged inputs, and insufficient observations.
- New tests pass Ruff 0.16.3; source/test formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Production-module Ruff diagnostics decrease from 43 to 41 when the old comprehensions are removed; there are no new diagnostics. The remaining pre-existing findings are unchanged.

The full harness suite and model benchmarks were not run. This corrects uncertainty aggregation and does not claim model-quality improvements.

## Related work

Checked all-state standard-deviation, stderr, overflow, and numerical-precision PR/issue searches; all 47 metric-file history entries; personal PR history; and all 142 current fork branches against the prior actual-commit audit. No matching implementation was found. The existing weighted group-uncertainty change concerns a separate aggregation of independent means. The earlier perplexity exponential-range fix handles unrepresentable exponentials; this change handles uncertainty for perplexities that are already finite.

entries.title: Keep prescription task choices consistent between prompts and scoring
entries.head: b87c7d6f4bfd95189964f72db49e9942b6f10ad9
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The prescription tasks call `doc_to_choice_easy` / `doc_to_choice_hard` while rendering the prompt and again while constructing log-likelihood requests. Each call samples new distractors. As a result, the scored negative continuations can differ from the options displayed to the model.

## Change

Sample both sets of choices once during `process_docs`, after selecting the gold answer and its position, and store them in the processed record. Rendering and request construction then read copies of those saved lists. The existing sampling rules and record-filtering logic are retained.

Both task configurations now resolve to version **1.2**. The README explains the corrected prompt/request consistency and the changed random-number consumption order. Version 1.2 scores should not be compared directly with version 1.1 results.

## Validation

The 13 new tests give **12 failures and 1 pass** on the base revision and **13 passes** with the fix:

- Native Dataset preprocessing for both difficulties and one to four source prescriptions.
- Exact agreement between displayed options and repeated choice callbacks, even after unrelated random draws.
- Both real YAML configurations loaded into `ConfigurableTask`; every constructed request is compared with the corresponding displayed option.
- Saving and reloading processed datasets preserves prompts and choices.
- Existing record filtering, gold membership, and gold position remain covered.

The tests use native dataset/task implementations and local synthetic records. No model inference or full-dataset benchmark was run, and no model accuracy improvement is claimed.

Ruff checks on the new test, formatting checks, YAML resolution, and `git diff --check` pass. The existing utility file still has the same nine Ruff diagnostics as the base revision (five `BLE001`, two `S110`, and two `UP032`); their codes and messages were compared against the base, with no new diagnostic introduced.

## Related work

The original task was added in #2714. The actual changes in #3589 (removing a prompt print) and #4041 (diagnosis-key validation) were checked; neither addresses repeated choice sampling.

entries.title: Return infinite perplexity when the exponential exceeds the float range
entries.head: 207e825dc0490a6cc49148f47abb22dea33a07be
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Both perplexity aggregations call `math.exp` on the mean negative log likelihood. A finite mean log loss above the representable exponential range raises `OverflowError`, interrupting evaluation aggregation. For example, normalized finite log probabilities from `log_softmax([0, -1000])` trigger this failure even though the scoring stage itself succeeds.

## Change

Return positive infinity when exponentiating the mean log loss overflows. Keep `math.exp` for representable results, preserve existing NaN and negative-infinite log-likelihood behavior, and leave mean/weight validation errors outside the exception handler.

This applies to both `perplexity` and `weighted_perplexity`, so word and byte perplexity also retain a reportable result. Infinite bootstrap replicates still have an undefined standard error (NaN).

## Validation

- Final unchanged source: **8 failed, 19 passed** in the 27 new regression/control cases.
- Patched source plus the complete existing `tests/test_metrics.py`: **35 passed**.
- An 80-digit Decimal reference covers ordinary values, the largest finite exponential boundary, and its next floating-point neighbor.
- Real `ConfigurableTask` processing and evaluator aggregation cover log-likelihood and rolling log-likelihood tasks, with bootstrap disabled and enabled. Input log probabilities come from native SciPy log-softmax; no model inference was run.
- Zero total weight continues to raise its existing error.
- New tests pass Ruff 0.16.3. Source/test formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The production metric module has the same 43 pre-existing Ruff diagnostics on the original and patched source, with identical codes and messages.

The full harness suite and model benchmarks were not run. This fixes aggregation completing at the floating-point range boundary; it does not change representable perplexities or improve model quality.

## Related work

Checked all-state perplexity/overflow PR and issue searches, the complete metric-file history, personal PR history, and all 141 current fork branches against the prior actual-commit audit. No matching implementation was found. The existing log-space bias-score change modifies separate demographic-bias tasks and does not handle perplexity aggregation.

entries.title: Stream request-cache serialization to reduce peak memory
entries.head: 0ec73a7605fd361dc03e32f1f5163253a009fddd
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Request-cache writes first materialize the entire pickle with `dill.dumps`, and reads first retain the complete file with `file.read()`. Large cached request collections therefore need an additional serialized-data-sized allocation alongside their actual objects.

## Change

Use dill's file interfaces (`dump` and `load`) to serialize and deserialize through the already-open binary file. Cache keys, file names, protocol defaults, directory creation, disabled-cache behavior, and exception-to-cache-miss handling stay the same. Existing cache files remain readable, and new cache bytes match the previous serializer.

## Validation

- Original implementation: **2 memory-regression failures, 10 semantic tests passed**.
- Patched implementation: **18 passed**, covering all 12 new tests and the complete existing `tests/test_cache.py` module.
- Existing dill protocols 3, 4, and 5, exact serialized bytes, `Instance` metadata and shared references, recursive/callable payloads, corrupt/missing/disabled caches are covered.
- A real `ConfigurableTask` builds requests, writes the cache, restores a limited request set in a fresh task, and processes a result successfully.
- Ruff 0.16.3 checks, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

### Local memory and timing

Measured on a shared CPU environment using one warmup and seven timed calls per case. Peak Python allocation was measured separately with `tracemalloc`. Every original/patched cache file has the same SHA-256, and every restored object equals its input.

| Payload | Original write peak | Patched write peak | Original read peak | Patched read peak |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 requests, roughly 1 KiB context each | 309,993 B | 201,400 B | 383,939 B | 272,020 B |
| 1,000 requests, roughly 8 KiB context each | 10,548,001 B | 1,446,916 B | 17,795,904 B | 9,507,308 B |
| Single 8 MiB byte payload | 9,445,476 B | 8,093 B | 16,784,941 B | 8,404,107 B |

For the 1,000-request fixture, median write time was 26.279 → 25.504 ms and read time was 2.312 → 2.021 ms. For the small 100-request fixture, write time was 2.322 → 2.366 ms and read time was 0.116 → 0.115 ms. The benefit is reduced serialization memory; small-cache latency is effectively unchanged in this measurement and is not claimed to improve universally.

These measurements cover cache I/O and serialization only. The full harness suite and model inference were not run. Request objects and dill's memo still occupy memory proportional to the cached data; the cache is not made lazy, and this change does not add atomic writes or change cache-key semantics.

## Related work

Checked all-state request-cache/serialization/dill/stream searches, all six actual source-history patches, personal PR history, and the actual pre-existing fork commits. The current 144 fork heads differ from the prior audit only by the already-published SCORE counting change. Existing file-name work (#4446 and #4547) and response-cache coalescing (#4588) address different paths and are not included here.

entries.title: Count SCORE answer agreement without enumerating every pair
entries.head: 1817b30352a92a73ce7520e1934c7d4219d5ff8f
entries.published_body:
## Problem

SCORE's exact-string consistency rate enumerates every pair of answers to a question. That performs quadratic Python work even though only the number of equal-answer pairs is needed. The same loop is used in prompt/option consistency and in the non-greedy log summarizer.

## Change

For each question, count how many times each answer has already appeared. An answer seen `k` times contributes exactly `k` additional matching pairs. This takes expected linear work in the number of responses and stores one count per distinct answer.

Keep the existing pair-count denominator, weighting between differently sized response groups, empty/singleton behavior, case/Unicode-sensitive equality, and the separate pairwise mathematical-equivalence scoring path. Scores do not change, so task versions stay unchanged.

## Validation

- **Original and patched source: 26 passed** in the new semantic tests. This is a performance change; the original implementation passes these correctness controls.
- Independent enumeration of all answer pairs covers empty/singleton groups, identical/distinct answers, uneven group sizes, randomized groups, response ordering, case, whitespace, Unicode, and a 900-response group. Inputs remain unchanged.
- The real MMLU-Pro SCORE YAML, `ConfigurableTask`, prompt expansion, result processing, and evaluator aggregation preserve consistency and per-prompt accuracy.
- The real non-greedy summarizer reads five seed-specific JSONL files and persists the expected consistency and per-seed accuracy.
- Existing numeric-equivalence scoring is exercised separately and unchanged.
- New tests, formatting of all changed Python files, and `git diff --check` pass Ruff 0.16.3. The two production modules retain their 16 and 7 pre-existing Ruff findings, with no new diagnostics.

### Local timing

One warmup followed by seven measured runs per case, reporting the median on a shared CPU environment, Python 3.12.14. Each question's answers cycle through four distinct strings. These measurements cover only consistency aggregation, excluding generation and file I/O.

| Questions | Responses per question | Original prompt CR | Patched prompt CR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10,000 | 5 | 5.512 ms | 2.458 ms |
| 10,000 | 10 | 20.462 ms | 4.389 ms |
| 1,000 | 100 | 205.332 ms | 4.019 ms |
| 100 | 1,000 | 2242.578 ms | 4.894 ms |

The non-greedy entry point was also timed and returned the same consistency value in every run. The change trades the pair iterator's constant auxiliary storage for a dictionary proportional to the number of distinct answers per question. It does not claim faster model inference or improved model quality; the full harness suite and model benchmarks were not run.

## Related work

Checked all-state consistency/counting/performance searches, the complete histories of both affected files, personal PR history, and all 143 current fork branches against the existing actual-commit audit. Read the actual patch of #4336: that fixes option-label remapping and does not change pair counting. This change preserves the current remapping behavior and is independent of that fix.

entries.title: perf: bound memory when selecting regex answer matches
entries.head: a4e9cf6d62b3c0da4f12393920fa975b8a19ffaa
entries.published_body:
## Summary

Regex answer extraction currently materializes every `findall` result before selecting `group_select`. A long response can therefore allocate a large list of captures even when only the first or last answer is needed.

Use `finditer` to stop at a nonnegative selected index, or retain only the required suffix in a bounded deque for negative indices. A shared helper reconstructs the existing zero-, one-, and multiple-capture `findall` return forms, including unmatched optional captures as empty strings. Both the primary regex filter and multiple-choice fallback use the same selection semantics.

No-match fallbacks, out-of-range index errors, zero-width advancement, capture stripping, and multiple-choice conversion retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

[Native CPU validation on the exact source commit](https://github.com/Afloat16/lm-evaluation-harness/actions/runs/43305454239) passes **146 tests**: 139 new cases plus the existing filter module. The new coverage includes independent `re.findall` comparisons, optional and empty groups, Unicode, zero-width matches, large positive/negative indices, multiple-choice fallbacks, and real `ConfigurableTask` request/filter/scoring integration.

Restoring the original extraction implementation produces **4 memory-limit failures and 135 passing semantic/control cases**. Ruff lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Allocation and timing measurements

The same-process benchmark runs the native original and patched `RegexFilter.apply`, with one warmup and nine measured calls per case. Allocation peaks are measured separately with `tracemalloc`; input-string construction is outside the measured region. Outputs are equal in every case.

For 100,000 six-digit matches in a 699,999-byte response:

| Selected match | Original median | Patched median | Original peak allocation | Patched peak allocation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First (0) | 15.992 ms | 0.002604 ms | 5,502,806 B | 2,500 B |
| Second (1) | 15.786 ms | 0.002544 ms | 5,502,806 B | 2,581 B |
| Last (-1) | 15.675 ms | 18.211 ms | 5,502,806 B | 4,117 B |
| Penultimate (-2) | 15.158 ms | 18.189 ms | 5,502,806 B | 4,253 B |

Negative indices still scan the whole response and are slower in this large-input benchmark; their benefit is bounded match storage. With only 32 matches, the penultimate case also has a small allocation increase (3,638 to 3,725 B) and a timing regression (0.005959 to 0.009053 ms). This change does not promise a speedup for every response or index.

These measurements cover extraction only, not model inference or overall evaluation throughput.

entries.title: Keep embedding data separate from model drift labels
entries.head: ebe4db657b68ac817411efb4b11a7e545fa4dbfb
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`ModelDriftMethod` writes a `target` column directly into each embedding DataFrame and then removes it from the classifier features. This mutates the caller's data and silently discards an existing embedding dimension named `target`. If the same DataFrame is supplied for both samples, the second assignment overwrites both sets of labels, so fitting fails with a single-class error.

## Change

Construct the domain-classification target as a separate array in the same reference/current order as the concatenated embeddings. Preserve all input dimensions and leave the original DataFrames unchanged. PCA, train/test splitting, classifier configuration, and drift threshold logic stay the same.

## Validation

Seven new tests cover input preservation with and without bootstrap/PCA, invariance under renaming an embedding dimension, and comparing a DataFrame with itself. On a fixture whose only separating dimension is named `target`, the old implementation reports ROC AUC 0.4125 and no drift; renaming that dimension yields AUC 1.0. The fix makes the result independent of that column name. This is a correctness example, not a general accuracy or performance claim.

- Baseline: 4 failures and 3 passing controls with the final regression tests.
- Fixed: all 7 new tests plus the existing native embedding-drift report test pass (8 total).
- Ruff 0.3.7 checks and formatting, plus `git diff --check`, pass.
- Tested on Python 3.12 with CPU dependencies. The complete repository suite and mypy were not run.

entries.title: Select MAPE near-zero rows without expanding duplicate index labels
entries.head: f56d36ee6a9061046c3abd2748c3a98ed375da47
entries.published_body:
## Problem

MAPE zero handling selects near-zero targets, then uses their index labels to drop or replace rows. With duplicate labels, `drop` also removes unrelated observations sharing those labels. On pandas 2.3, `replace` raises `InvalidIndexError` instead of producing the report.

For targets `[0, 1, 2, 0, 4, 8]`, predictions `[2, 2, 1, 3, 6, 8]`, and index `[7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9]`, dropping the two near-zero target rows should produce MAPE 50%. The current code drops four rows and reports 25%.

## Change

Keep the boolean near-zero mask and use it directly for both row filtering and replacement. This preserves the individual observations even when their index labels are repeated, including MultiIndex labels.

The zero threshold, replacement value, denominator formula, and `near_zero_values` counter are unchanged. In particular, this is separate from #1933 (the near-zero row counter) and #1986 (negative-target denominators).

## Validation

- Eleven new regression cases: base code has 8 failures and 3 passing controls.
- Fixed code: 12 tests pass including the existing native regression-report smoke test.
- Tests cover duplicate integer/string/MultiIndex labels, unique-label controls, hand-calculated mean and sample standard deviation, unchanged input frames, and `none` handling.
- Native `Report([MAPE(...)])` calls verify that changing only row labels does not change the reported metric.
- Pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format checks and `git diff --check` pass.

The full repository test suite was not run. This change corrects selection of evaluation rows; it does not claim improved model prediction quality.

entries.title: Handle zero median bandwidth in embedding MMD drift
entries.head: 95778276ac6b18c6ce35e1b80d41b4bafca2f367
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Constant or heavily repeated embeddings can have a zero median pairwise distance. The embedding MMD method then passes `gamma=1/0` to its RBF kernel, producing NaN entries and a NaN drift score. The same failure occurs in the bootstrap reference kernel when the reference embeddings are constant, even when the current embeddings differ.

## Change

Use the zero-bandwidth limit of the RBF kernel when the estimated squared bandwidth is exactly zero: equal vectors have kernel value 1 and distinct vectors have value 0. Group equal vectors with `np.unique`, then compare their group labels, avoiding a samples-by-samples-by-features intermediate. Positive bandwidths keep the existing `pairwise_kernels` calculation.

Both the observed embedding kernel and its bootstrap reference kernel use this helper. This change is confined to `legacy/metrics/data_drift/embedding_drift_methods.py`; it does not change the separate univariate `mmd_stattest.py` distance calculation addressed in #1966.

## Validation

- Identical constant embeddings return a finite zero score with and without bootstrap, including nonzero constant values.
- A changed constant embedding is still detected; its score matches `2 * (1 - exp(-1))`.
- A repeated-vector example with zero median bandwidth matches a hand-counted unbiased MMD statistic, preserving distinct groups.
- A positive-bandwidth control matches an independently constructed RBF statistic.
- The final eight new tests fail 6/pass 2 before the change; all eight pass after it. The existing native embedding-drift report test also passes (9 total).
- Ruff 0.3.7 checks and formatting, plus `git diff --check`, pass.

The full repository suite and mypy were not run. This resolves undefined kernel values for degenerate bandwidths; it does not establish a general detection-quality improvement or change bootstrap sample-size policy.

entries.title: Stratify the train/test split for model-based embedding drift
entries.head: b5232cb5e7cf530e6a70e70df34abfe5d26dec9f
entries.published_body:
## Problem

ModelDriftMethod creates a binary source label for reference/current embeddings, then uses an unstratified 50/50 split. Even when both populations contain at least two rows, the fixed random split can leave the training set with one class. For example, reference/current sizes 2/8 and 3/4 raise SGDClassifier's single-class error. Training the classifier and evaluating its ROC AUC both require the source classes to remain represented.

## Change

Stratify train_test_split by the existing source labels, preserving the 50/50 ratio, shuffle setting, random seed, classifier, and thresholds. This change is independent of the separate fix for using an embedding dimension named target.

## Validation

- 10 new tests on the upstream base: 5 failed, 5 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing embedding-drift Report test: 11 passed on CPU.
- Cases cover small imbalanced samples in both directions, a balanced control, bootstrap and fixed-threshold decisions, an explicit stratified SGD/ROC reference, and a real Report integration control.
- The tests restore the caller's NumPy random state so the existing bootstrap behavior cannot contaminate other tests.
- Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

Stratification can change numeric scores on existing datasets because it changes which rows enter each split. This does not provide a statistically reliable drift estimate from arbitrarily small datasets: each population must have enough rows for both splits. The Report plotting layer's independent t-SNE/KDE sample requirements are unchanged; the Report control uses a sufficient sample size.

entries.title: Load training files in a stable order across ranks
entries.head: e7b4a33f0924f666d665bdebb2fdbf66b7285cd2
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Directory-backed embedder and reranker training load JSON/JSONL files in the order returned by `os.listdir`. That order can differ between hosts even when every host has the same files and the training seed is identical.

This changes concatenated row indices and capped per-file sampling. For same-dataset training, ranks can therefore combine examples from different datasets in one global batch and duplicate or omit rows across the epoch.

## Change

Sort directory entries in the three training loaders before loading or sampling files. Preserve the caller's `train_data` order and the existing JSON/JSONL filtering.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/test_finetune_file_order.py tests/test_finetune_trainer_compat.py -q --tb=short`: 11 passed.

The seven new regression cases fail on unchanged master and pass with this patch. They exercise the real dataset constructors and local JSONL data under reversed directory listings:

- Stable concatenated rows in the embedder, same-dataset embedder and reranker loaders, both with and without per-file sample caps.
- Two rank-specific same-dataset configurations with opposite file enumeration orders, checking that each combined batch belongs to one dataset and every input row is covered exactly once.

The four existing trainer compatibility tests also pass. Ruff check and formatting pass for the new tests, and `git diff --check` passes.

Validation used Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu, Transformers 4.57.1 and Datasets 5.0.1. The rank test exercises dataset partitioning locally; a distributed GPU training job was not run.

entries.title: Preserve the caller's NumPy random state during embedding drift bootstrap
entries.head: e5765ce77619ec08b91c40c5ccc7c04578a3a66c
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Embedding distance and MMD bootstrap repeatedly call `np.random.seed(i)` and draw from the process-global generator. The model-based drift bootstrap does the same through `calc_roc_auc_random`. Running a drift check therefore changes the random sequence used by later training, sampling, or evaluation code in the same process.

## Change

Use a local `np.random.RandomState(i)` for each bootstrap repetition and for the random-AUC helper. Keep the same seeds, legacy generator algorithm, draw order, bootstrap samples, and threshold calculations. The change isolates the generator rather than changing the statistical procedure.

## Validation

- Twelve new native regression tests: base code has 6 failures and 6 passing controls.
- Fixed code: 13 tests pass including the existing embedding-drift report smoke test.
- All three drift methods are checked with bootstrap enabled and disabled. Tests compare the caller's subsequent random draws against an untouched generator.
- Random AUC values match an independently seeded reference for seeds 0, 17 and 99.
- Repeated bootstrap results remain independent of the external NumPy seed.
- Each test restores the global state it found, so the checks do not change later tests' random state.
- Pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.

This concerns the embedding-drift bootstrap paths. It is separate from #1985, which changes the permutation implementation under `legacy/calculations/stattests/utils.py`. The full repository suite and end-to-end training benchmarks were not run.

entries.title: Reuse cumulative counts when building classification tables
entries.head: 937658c9f77003507a9a1f4d0c969fb3e835f7e0
entries.published_body:
## Problem

calculate_pr_table and calculate_lift_table recompute true-positive counts from the start of the sorted population at every percentile. This repeatedly scans approximately 20 and 100 overlapping prefixes, respectively, even though each table advances monotonically through the same binary target sequence.

## Change

Accumulate TP counts only over the newly included interval. Keep sorting, stable tie order, percentile boundaries, thresholds, rounding and returned rows unchanged. The change uses only the current interval slice rather than allocating a full-length cumulative-count array.

## Validation

- 28 new numerical and integration cases pass on both the original and changed implementations; this is a performance change, not a numerical bug fix.
- With the four existing classification calculation tests: 32 passed on CPU.
- Coverage includes empty/singleton inputs, percentile boundary sizes, non-divisible tails, tied scores, and native binary/multiclass current/reference Reports. Expected rows independently sum their selected populations.
- Repository-pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

Local CPU benchmark, one warm-up and five timed calls per case, seeded shuffled binary targets and scores, including each function's sorting but excluding construction/copying of its input list:

| Input rows | PR table before/after | Lift table before/after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10,000 | 2.729 / 1.576 ms | 8.585 / 2.758 ms |
| 100,000 | 31.454 / 18.258 ms | 101.109 / 20.950 ms |
| 500,000 | 642.536 / 138.943 ms | 1293.687 / 129.687 ms |

These are median local measurements, not end-to-end Report or training benchmarks. Every benchmark returned an identical table representation before and after. Sorting still determines the overall O(N log N) complexity; the change eliminates repeated target-prefix scans. The full repository and notebook smoke suites were not run.

entries.title: Keep unprompted same-dataset training text unchanged
entries.head: fb9dd25e52f0c265abba328eff22b7b866ed6a76
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Same-dataset training always formats the query instruction even when `query_instruction_for_retrieval` is left at its default `None`. With the default format, a query becomes `None<query text>`. Symmetric STS/clustering passages receive the same unintended prefix, and the ICL dataset repeats the behavior before tokenization. This introduces training text that is absent from the unprompted inference path.

The defect was found through code inspection and reproduced using the normal dataset constructors, local JSONL training data and a real local tokenizer.

## Change

Only format a resolved instruction when it is not `None`, for both base and ICL same-dataset training. Preserve explicit empty-string instructions, configured formats, per-row overrides, passage instructions on retrieval tasks and the ICL suffix/truncation behavior.

## Validation

`PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/test_finetune_optional_instructions.py tests/test_finetune_trainer_compat.py -q --tb=short`: 28 passed.

The 24 new cases produce 6 failures and 18 passes on unchanged master, then all pass with this patch. They cover the base and ICL datasets, retrieval/STS/clustering data, absent/global/per-row/empty instructions, queries and passages, and teacher-score/negative-group controls. No mocked package imports or pretrained downloads are used. The four existing trainer compatibility tests also pass. The new test file passes Ruff check and formatting; `git diff --check` passes.

Validation used Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu, Transformers 4.57.1 and Datasets 5.0.1. This verifies dataset text preparation; it does not claim retrieval-quality or GPU-training gains.

entries.title: Preserve reranker query groups in partial training batches
entries.head: 54ac9d565ed4ee287a4abb98bb75513d5cc4bf07
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The reranker collators flatten each query's positive and negative passages, but the model reshapes their scores using the configured training batch size. A final DataLoader batch with fewer queries can therefore mix candidates from different queries, raise a reshape error, or create one-candidate groups with zero cross-entropy. The same grouping also affects teacher targets and layerwise distillation.

## Changes

- Preserve the number of passages per query as `group_size` in both reranker collators.
- Infer the actual local query count from the encoded score rows and that group size in the shared and layerwise reranker training forwards.
- Keep the configured batch-size fallback for direct callers that omit the new metadata.
- Add native, download-free regression tests using tiny BERT, GPT-2, and the repository's LayerWiseMiniCPM models with real collators and DataLoader batches.

The group-size metadata stays valid when tensors are split at complete query-group boundaries. This change does not address existing DataParallel behavior for Python-list teacher scores or tensor splits through the middle of a query group.

## Validation

- On the unchanged upstream base, the 27 new cases produce **15 failures and 12 passes**; with this patch all **27 pass**.
- The tests compare cross-entropy, external distillation, and layerwise self-distillation losses and gradients against explicit per-query calculations, including one-query/two-query final batches, full batches, and legacy direct calls.
- Six additional cases within that set simulate per-device tensor splitting with replicated scalar metadata for all three model families.
- New tests plus existing Trainer/import and offline tokenizer-compatibility tests: **39 passed, 1 skipped** on PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu and Transformers 4.57.1. The skipped import check requires Transformers 5.x. Download-dependent model/tokenizer tests and CUDA execution were not run.
- Ruff on the new test file and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Avoid cross-query score matrices for local-negative training
entries.head: efeca600b61fa87fbe3da039bd31b9311bd981f2
entries.published_body:
## Problem

When dense embedder training disables in-batch negatives, the default local-scoring path still builds scores for every query against every passage and then selects each query's own passage group. For B queries and G passages per query, this materializes a B × (B × G) matrix although the objective uses only B × G entries.

## Changes

The three built-in dense embedder models use their existing batched similarity operation to compute each query's own passage group directly. The abstract embedder's two-dimensional scoring contract stays unchanged. Explicit scoring callbacks and dense subclasses that override `compute_score` retain the original path, so the optimization does not add a new shape requirement to custom models.

This is separate from #1609, which corrects M3 local-target and ensemble layouts. This patch leaves those loss and M3 callback paths unchanged.

## Validation

- The 31 new cases produce **2 allocation failures and 29 passes** on the unchanged base, and **31 passes** after this patch.
- Compare local scores and embedding gradients with independent per-query dot products in float32/float64, including non-contiguous tensors.
- Native tiny BERT, GPT-2 and decoder ICL training preserves supervised/KL losses and parameter gradients, with and without MRL. Native forward gradient comparisons use float64; the existing MRL float32 loss accumulator is retained.
- Custom callbacks, a custom two-dimensional abstract embedder, and custom scoring overrides of all three dense model classes keep their existing behavior.
- CPU profiling at B=128, G=8, D=16 shows the largest operator allocation in local scoring falling from **524,288 to 4,096 bytes** for float32 and from **1,048,576 to 8,192 bytes** for float64. These figures cover this scoring operation, not total model memory or GPU throughput.
- New tests plus existing Trainer/import modules: **39 passed, 1 skipped** on PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu and Transformers 4.57.1. The skipped check requires Transformers 5.x. No pretrained checkpoint or CUDA benchmark was used.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Train all requested layerwise reranker heads
entries.head: 159723be41f80ba4222abf2afb7509c2aa686487
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The layerwise training wrapper records `start_layer` but does not pass `cutoff_layers` to its backbone. The backbone defaults to returning only the final layer. As a result, intermediate layer scores never reach the training loss: their supervised loss is missing, the self-distillation loop has no student layers, and independent intermediate classifier heads receive no gradients.

## Changes

Pass the complete requested range, from `start_layer` through `num_hidden_layers`, when the training wrapper encodes pairs. The existing loss already supports multiple layer outputs, so no loss formula or backbone default needs to change. This also restores the layer selection used by the repository's earlier research training implementation in the current package entry point.

## Validation

- A real, locally initialized three-layer `LayerWiseMiniCPMForCausalLM` exercises shared and independent heads, three starting layers, external teacher targets, and self-distillation.
- Compare every returned score, the full loss, and parameter gradients with explicit backbone calls for the requested cutoff layers; check that each requested independent head receives nonzero gradients.
- Evaluation returns the requested layer scores with no training loss. Direct backbone calls still default to the final layer.
- The 20 new cases produce **12 failures and 8 passes** on the unchanged upstream base and **20 passes** with this patch.
- New cases plus existing Trainer/import compatibility modules: **28 passed, 1 skipped** with PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu and Transformers 4.57.1. The skipped check requires Transformers 5.x. These tests require no checkpoint download; pretrained retrieval quality and CUDA execution were not evaluated.
- Ruff on the new tests and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Include missing retrieval queries in evaluation averages
entries.head: d94a46fa298cf5baf5162c7c771cd9831d0cc62f
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`evaluate_metrics` averages the scores returned by pytrec_eval over the number of queries present in that output. A judged query omitted from a retrieval run disappears from the denominator, so an incomplete run can report perfect NDCG, MAP, recall and precision. Representing the same missing query with an explicit empty result instead gives a different score. A completely empty run also divides by zero even when the judgment set is nonempty.

## Changes

Average these four metrics over the full set of queries in `qrels`, matching the evaluation population already used by this module's MRR and capped recall. Missing query results contribute zero without changing per-query pytrec_eval calculations or complete-run scores.

## Validation

- Eleven native pytrec_eval cases cover omitted/empty/nonrelevant result equivalence, multiple cutoffs, entirely empty runs, hand-calculated rank-two hits, unjudged query exclusion, and complete-run controls.
- Exact baseline: **5 failed, 6 passed**. With the patch: **11 passed**.
- New cases plus existing Trainer/import checks: **19 passed, 1 skipped**; the skipped check requires Transformers 5.x.
- Tested with pytrec-eval-terrier 0.5.11 and FAISS CPU 1.16.0 installed. The tests use normal package imports and skip when these optional evaluation dependencies are unavailable.
- The judgment set remains nonempty in this regression scope; this change does not redefine empty-qrels behavior or other metric functions.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Handle empty evaluation reranking candidates
entries.head: fa7da1ec822e9f120370e695947204471fccb3e2
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`EvalReranker` always calls its scoring model, including when no query-document pairs remain. An empty retrieval run, zero reranking depth, or identical-ID filtering that removes all candidates reaches `AbsReranker.compute_score([])` and raises an `IndexError` before evaluation can continue.

## Changes

If the final pair list is empty, return an empty score mapping for each input query. Mixed batches that still contain candidates continue through the normal scoring path.

## Validation

- Eight regression cases use a locally saved tiny BERT classifier and vocabulary through the actual `BaseReranker` and evaluation wrapper.
- Cover no queries, one/multiple empty candidate lists, all candidates removed by identical-ID filtering, zero reranking depth, and mixed empty/nonempty query groups.
- Exact final baseline: **6 failed, 2 passed**. After the patch: **8 passed**.
- New cases plus existing Trainer/import tests: **16 passed, 1 skipped**. The skipped check requires Transformers 5.x.
- PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu, Transformers 4.57.1, FAISS CPU 1.16.0 and pytrec-eval-terrier 0.5.11; no remote checkpoint download or GPU run. Optional evaluation imports are skipped if their dependencies are absent; they were present for validation.
- This patch only handles an empty candidate set at the evaluation-wrapper boundary. Input candidate mutation and filtering depth remain separate behavior.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Preserve representable tail probabilities in the proportion z-test
entries.head: ab2a23a41ae5d8de1c5436153f8bc67bd42bb1ea
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The proportion z-test computes right-tail probabilities by subtracting norm.cdf from 1. At large positive z statistics, the CDF rounds to 1 even though the tail probability is representable, so the result becomes zero. This loses the reported p-value and can change drift decisions at small custom thresholds. For two binary populations of 500 rows with proportions 0.4 and 0.7, the two-sided p-value is approximately 1.50427e-21; the current result is zero.

## Change

Use norm.sf for the two-sided and greater alternatives. The mathematical test and threshold comparison remain the same, and the less alternative is unchanged.

## Validation

- 18 new tests on the upstream base: 10 failed, 8 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the two existing z-test cases: 20 passed on CPU.
- Independent math.erfc references cover positive, negative, zero, and tail statistics for every alternative, with zero absolute tolerance so a zero p-value cannot pass as a tiny nonzero value.
- Actual categorical Series cover both population orders and thresholds on either side of the expected p-value. A native ValueDrift Report verifies the reported result.
- Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This improves tail-probability accuracy. It does not imply a different decision at conventional thresholds such as 0.05, or prevent underflow for probabilities below the floating-point range. The full repository suite was not run.

entries.title: Preserve retrieval candidates when evaluating rerankers
entries.head: ba599e0562ab5839584956dbd8209aab1185d18e
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`EvalReranker` replaces each query's candidate mapping in the supplied `search_results` dictionary with a truncated top-k mapping. Reusing the same retrieval results for another reranker or depth silently loses candidates: a top-1 run followed by top-3 can only rerank the one candidate left by the first call.

## Changes

Build the top-k candidate mappings locally without modifying the caller's retrieval results. Ranking, truncation, identical-ID filtering, and score computation keep their existing order and behavior.

## Validation

- Eight native regression cases use a tiny BERT sequence classifier and local BERT vocabulary saved to disk, then run the actual `BaseReranker` inference path through `EvalReranker`.
- Check the original result values and nested mappings, top-1/top-2/top-4 selections with identical-ID filtering on/off, and comparisons at increasing/decreasing reranking depths.
- Exact final baseline: **7 failed, 1 passed**. After the patch: **8 passed**.
- New cases plus existing Trainer/import checks: **16 passed, 1 skipped**. The skipped check requires Transformers 5.x.
- Tested with PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu, Transformers 4.57.1, FAISS CPU 1.16.0 and pytrec-eval-terrier 0.5.11. Tests skip cleanly when optional evaluation dependencies are absent; they were present for these runs. No remote model download or GPU execution was used.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

entries.title: Apply an explicitly configured zero relevance threshold
entries.head: 9973c22e8b8ea46cbbe8a7a2681cda1991dd3f1b
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The shared recommendation preprocessing uses a truthiness check for min_rel_score. An explicitly configured zero threshold is skipped, so items with a zero rating are treated as irrelevant. This can also exclude users who should have relevant feedback and changes the resulting recommendation metrics.

## Change

Apply the threshold whenever min_rel_score is not None, including zero. Preserve the existing >= comparison, optional binary conversion, and no-feedback-user policy. Other threshold values and the unconfigured behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

- 20 new cases on the upstream base: 8 failed, 12 passed.
- All recommendation metric tests with the fix: 58 passed on CPU.
- Direct preprocessing cases cover None, negative, zero and positive thresholds with both binary/graded data and both no-feedback policies; input frames are unchanged.
- Native current/reference Report cases check Precision, Recall, Hit Rate, MRR and NDCG against hand-calculated values for three users, with both scores and explicit ranks.
- Repository-pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This corrects the handling of an explicit zero threshold in the existing recommendation preprocessing. It does not change ranking, tie handling, metric formulas, or the meaning of a missing threshold. The full repository and notebook smoke suites were not run.

entries.title: Preserve text class labels in classification lift tables
entries.head: 44d54049cb4603b95e8cbff4c626910268ff4e3f
entries.published_body:
## Problem

ClassificationLiftTable converts probability column labels to int in both the binary and multiclass paths. Valid text classes such as cat/dog or Unicode labels raise ValueError before the report can be produced. PredictionData, the result schema, and the renderer already support text labels, and ClassificationPRTable already preserves them.

## Change

Use the original class labels as lift-table keys. Leave target binarization, table calculations, rendering, and the existing numeric-key JSON deserialization behavior unchanged.

## Validation

- 15 new tests against the upstream base: 12 failed, 3 passed.
- The fixed tests and the existing report JSON test: 16 passed on CPU.
- Binary and multiclass English/Unicode labels match equivalent integer-encoded tables; independent assertions check the final TP/FP counts, precision, recall, and lift values.
- Native legacy Report cases cover current/reference data, JSON round trips, renderer tabs, and unchanged input frames.
- Integer-key JSON round trips remain covered.
- Repository-pinned Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This corrects text-label handling in the legacy classification lift-table metric. It does not change lift formulas or the existing normalization of numeric-looking dictionary keys. The full repository and notebook smoke suites were not run.

entries.title: Align M3 ColBERT vectors and masks across variable-length sub-batches
entries.head: 9a2dd61e9a47464b361abd58a1f8d5d1a363012a
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Both embedder collators can dynamically pad each sub-batch to a different sequence length. M3's list-input encoding path directly concatenates the ColBERT vectors along the batch dimension, so unified fine-tuning raises a tensor-size mismatch when those sequence lengths differ. This prevents the documented sub-batch option from working on ordinary variable-length training text.

## Changes

Pad the ColBERT vectors to the longest sub-batch sequence before concatenation, using the tokenizer's padding side and zero vectors for padding. Build the corresponding list-input attention mask in the same order: remove each sub-batch's first position, as ColBERT encoding already does, then pad. A leading column preserves the existing full-mask scoring interface.

Dense-only encoding and the tensor-input sub-batch path are unchanged.

## Validation

Added 20 tests with an actual local BertTokenizerFast, tiny BERT backbone, sparse/ColBERT heads, and both native collators:

- Dynamic sub-batch embeddings match the existing full-batch path with right padding.
- Supervised, teacher-distillation, and self-distillation training match full-batch losses and all parameter gradients.
- Left/right padding preserves each original vector and aligns every mask value with it, with zero vectors and zero masks in added positions.
- Dense-only and fixed-length tensor sub-batches retain their previous behavior.

The unchanged upstream base produces **14 failed, 6 passed**. With the fix, the new tests and existing Trainer/import checks produce **28 passed, 1 skipped**. Ruff on the new test module and `git diff --check` pass.

The tests preserve the existing first-position removal convention and do not claim to redefine left-padded special-token handling. This change is separate from passage MaxSim masking in #1610; it does not change that scoring reduction.

entries.title: Keep embedding bootstrap samples large enough for their statistics
entries.head: 682dd1c7da2cbc57d122e9a60ab5e1899325f7df
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Distance and MMD embedding drift choose bootstrap sample sizes by truncating population-proportional counts. For small or imbalanced inputs, this can produce zero observations for a mean, or one observation for the unbiased MMD statistic whose denominator contains n*(n-1).

The empty mean makes Euclidean distance raise on NaN input; cityblock distance instead produces a NaN threshold and reports no drift. MMD raises ZeroDivisionError. This also affects substantial imbalanced datasets: native Reports fail for reference/current sizes 20/500 with distance and 20/200 with MMD.

## Change

Apply the minimum sample count required by each statistic to both bootstrap subsamples: one for distance between means, and two for unbiased MMD. The bootstrap already samples with replacement. Preserve the proportional counts whenever they are large enough, the seeds, the statistic formulas, bandwidths, and quantile settings.

## Validation

- 24 new tests on the upstream base: 10 failed, 14 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing embedding-drift Report test: 25 passed on CPU.
- Independent mean-distance and pairwise RBF U-statistic references verify scores and seeded bootstrap decisions. Cases cover small/imbalanced inputs, sufficient-size and non-bootstrap controls, the cityblock NaN decision, and native Reports for both methods.
- Tests restore the caller's global NumPy random state.
- Ruff 0.3.7 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This fixes the bootstrap subsample domain. It does not relax the original input requirements (MMD still needs at least two observations in each population), solve degenerate bandwidths, or establish reliable inference from arbitrarily small samples. The full repository suite was not run.

entries.title: Apply retrieval and reranking depth after candidate filtering
entries.head: ec20b74c9aa506553d522d8094431044aa081d8e
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The configured search or reranking depth is applied before excluded candidates are removed. Dense retrieval can return fewer eligible documents when a query ID also occurs in the corpus. BRIGHT retrieval has the same issue for its per-query exclusion lists, and reranking can discard a valid candidate at the depth boundary when an identical ID occupies an earlier slot.

## Changes

- Retrieve one additional dense candidate when identical IDs are excluded, then cap the eligible output at the requested depth.
- For BRIGHT, retrieve enough candidates for the largest relevant exclusion list (plus an optional identical ID), bounded by the corpus size. Keep the existing `N/A` sentinel behavior.
- Remove identical IDs from the reranker candidate sequence before selecting its configured depth.

## Validation

Added 30 tests using local tiny BERT models, the native embedder/reranker, and FAISS. Retrieval results are compared with a full NumPy similarity ranking after applying the same eligibility rules. Cases cover depths 1, 2, and larger than the corpus; multiple BRIGHT exclusions; queries with and without corpus IDs; and enabled/disabled identical-ID filtering.

- New tests against the unchanged upstream base: **14 failed, 16 passed**.
- New tests with this change plus the existing Trainer/import checks: **38 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Ruff on the new test module and `git diff --check` passed.

This change fixes candidate selection depth. It does not change embedding scores, reranking scores, or exclusion policy.

entries.title: Keep fully masked DFT and EAFT losses differentiable
entries.head: 7f66140c5d71abced36e821fb083a4a5be49c606
entries.published_body:
# What does this PR do?

DFT and EAFT return a newly constructed zero tensor when every shifted label is ignored. The value is zero, but it is detached from the model: calling `backward()` raises `RuntimeError: element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn`. This can interrupt fine-tuning on a fully masked microbatch.

Return the sum of the unreduced cross-entropy loss that has already been computed. Ignored positions contribute zero, and this sum retains the autograd connection to the logits. A fully masked microbatch therefore produces zero parameter gradients. The valid-token weighting and normalization paths are unchanged.

## Validation

- Added 10 native CPU regression cases through the public DFT/EAFT loss functions: the upstream base has 8 failures and 2 passes; this patch passes all 10.
- FP32 and BF16, sequence lengths 1 and 4, a real `Linear` model and SGD step: backward completes, gradients are exactly zero, and parameters remain unchanged.
- Adding an ignored sequence to a valid batch preserves the valid loss and gradients.
- Command: `WANDB_DISABLED=true python -m pytest tests/train/test_masked_finetuning_losses.py -q`.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including the pinned Ruff 0.15.5 checks and formatting, pass. License checks, compileall, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The final tests also pass with the normal root conftest under PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu and its matching TorchAudio/TorchVision packages (10 passed). The full suite and GPU training were not run.

entries.title: Count supervised token positions in LD-DPO
entries.head: efa2e93ff3fd585f0bc513437259c63b95516c84
entries.published_body:
# What does this PR do?

LD-DPO computes the shared response length from the number of supervised tokens in each chosen/rejected pair. Its prefix mask currently uses raw sequence offsets, so ignored tokens inside a response consume that shared-length budget. Later supervised tokens are then discounted too early. This affects labels with internal ignored spans, including the control-token masks produced by the MOSS-VL input postprocessor.

Build the prefix mask from cumulative supervised-token positions in both the legacy helper and the v1 trainer. The v1 chosen and rejected segments count their own supervised tokens independently. The first `min(chosen_length, rejected_length)` supervised tokens retain full weight; only the remaining supervised tokens receive `ld_alpha`. Ignored tokens still contribute nothing. Contiguous responses and the existing `ld_alpha=None` path retain their behavior.

## Validation

- 55 new native CPU regression cases: 29 legacy cases have **13 failures / 16 passes** on unchanged upstream; 26 v1 cases have **9 failures / 17 passes**. The complete patch passes **55/55**.
- An independent ordered-token reference checks log probabilities and every logit gradient for contiguous responses, internal ignored positions, unequal prompt offsets, float32/float64, and alpha `None`, `0`, `0.25`, and `1`.
- A locally initialized GPT-2 and the real `CustomDPOTrainer` check preference loss, gradients, and two SGD updates against an independent DPO calculation for one and two pairs.
- The real `MossVLPlugin.post_process_mossvl_inputs` supplies control-token masks to the loss helper using a local tokenizer and processor metadata. This does not require downloading a vision model.
- v1 coverage checks packed chosen/rejected segments, independently shifted/internal ignored labels, both segment orders, and the `use_ld=False` reference path. Real GPT-2 logits, gradients and two SGD updates agree with an ordered-token reference.
- New regressions plus the three existing v1 DPO precision tests and MOSS-VL plugin test: **59 passed**.
- Command: `WANDB_DISABLED=true python -m pytest tests/train/test_ld_dpo_token_positions.py tests_v1/trainers/test_v1_ld_dpo_token_positions.py tests_v1/trainers/test_dpo_loss_precision.py tests/data/test_mm_plugin.py::test_moss_vl_plugin -q`.
- The normal repository root conftest loads with PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu, matching TorchVision/TorchAudio, Transformers 4.57.1, and TRL 0.24.0. Four pre-existing TRL `padding_value` deprecation warnings are emitted.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks, the repository license check, and `git diff --check` pass. The full repository suite, GPU/distributed training, and an end-to-end vision model run were not executed.

entries.title: Preserve the batch axis in reward model predictions
entries.head: 6dc20619b135803fb563df62c0e341b24a2c72b0
entries.published_body:
# What does this PR do?

Reward model evaluation gathers one chosen and one rejected score per pair as tensors of shape `[batch, 1]`.
