entries.title: Reset sentiment negation and modifiers at unordered term boundaries
entries.head: 06c0c1c5bb3674d367f5bfcec49dc089a45967da
entries.published_body:
## Problem
Sentiment's dictionary and term-document paths insert `(None, None)` separators to prevent negation and degree modifiers from linking unrelated bag-of-words terms. `assessments` currently skips those separators without resetting its preceding-word state. The same word weights can therefore produce different scores when their insertion order changes: with the bundled English lexicon, `{"not": 1, "good": 1}` has polarity -0.35 while the reverse ordering has polarity +0.7.

## Change
Clear the pending modifier and negation at an explicit `None` boundary. Ordered word sequences continue to apply the same negation and modifier rules. The change is limited to those two states; it does not redefine punctuation-specific assessment rules.

## Validation
- The 11 new tests on unchanged upstream: 9 failed, 2 passed.
- New tests and all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 15 passed, 1 deselected, with native package imports.
- Tests use hand-calculated weighted polarity/subjectivity, four term orders, both supported bag representations, the bundled English lexicon, and ordered `not good`/`very good` controls.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.
- Corpus-dependent classifier tests were not included; this change needs no downloaded NLTK corpus.

entries.title: Preserve the positive class prior when updating training data
entries.head: 77d1217fc40afcf965b11b5a91a65679945c1afa
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`PositiveNaiveBayesClassifier.update()` silently replaces an existing positive-class prior with 0.5 when the caller only adds training data. A classifier initialized with a prior of 0.2 therefore changes its prior to 0.5 on an ordinary update. This also changes its learned posterior probabilities. The defect was found through code inspection and reproduced with actual NLTK training.

## Change

Preserve the current prior when `positive_prob_prior` is omitted or `None`. Continue to accept an explicit new prior, including on later updates. The constructor's default remains 0.5. Document the update behavior and add the contributor entry requested by the contribution guide.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_positive_classifier_prior.py tests/test_formats.py tests/test_utils.py -q`: 27 passed.
- The 10 new regression cases on unchanged dev: 9 failed, 1 passed; with the fix: all 10 pass.
- Regressions train real NLTK models on tokenized documents and compare the updated posteriors with fresh training at the intended prior. They cover positive-only, unlabeled-only, combined and empty updates, explicit prior replacement, subsequent updates and the default prior.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check and `git diff --check`: passed.

Python 3.12.14, NLTK 3.10.4, pytest 9.2.0. The broader corpus-dependent classifier tests could not complete because `punkt_tab` is unavailable and NLTK's downloader rejects this environment's proxy. The new tests require no downloaded corpora.

entries.title: Retain single-pass classifier training rows and token sequences
entries.head: 54bf0503ef5a020a7ea01e7448441b2f36a6db06
entries.published_body:
## Problem
Classifier training reads its dataset once to build the vocabulary and again to extract features. A single-pass row iterator is exhausted by the first read, and single-pass token sequences become empty documents. During `update`, list extension consumes a row iterator before its new vocabulary is collected. These cases produce missing training data or silently empty features.

## Change
Materialize training rows and non-string token sequences once before the existing repeated reads, both on construction and update. Strings keep their tokenizer path. Retraining and the underlying NLTK algorithms are unchanged.

## Validation
- The final 16 new tests on unchanged upstream: 12 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus existing format and utility tests: 33 passed.
- Actual NaiveBayes and DecisionTree training cover outer row lists/iterators and inner token lists/iterators. A hand-built feature matrix verifies retained vocabulary and observations; updated predictions are compared with a fresh model trained from equivalent reusable data.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.
- Broader corpus-dependent classifier tests remain limited by unavailable NLTK data; all new cases use the supported pretokenized input path.

entries.title: Forward probability estimators when training positive classifiers
entries.head: 8db148dd403d359cda5f1383a7c81c325e4c3fe8
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`PositiveNaiveBayesClassifier.train` accepts additional arguments but discards them when calling NLTK. Passing a custom probability estimator therefore silently trains with the default smoothing. The existing `update` method already forwards these options.

## Change
Forward the extra arguments after the configured positive prior, consistently with `update`, and document that order. Add real NLTK probability-distribution comparisons for positional and keyword estimators while retaining the configured prior.

## Validation
- The 13 new tests on unchanged upstream: 8 failed, 5 passed.
- New tests plus existing format and utility tests: 30 passed.
- Lidstone smoothing with gamma 0.1, 0.5 and 2.0 is compared against direct NLTK training at priors 0.2 and 0.5, across several query feature sets. Default ELE smoothing is a control.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Preserve sentiment scores and assessments across serialization
entries.head: 24fe0fcdd4b2910f1ae0226e0d742cf790353a33
entries.published_body:
## Problem
The `Score` tuple returned by the lexical sentiment engine requires two constructor arguments. Its inherited tuple pickle/copy behavior supplies a single tuple instead, so modern pickle protocols and both shallow/deep copying raise `TypeError` rather than preserving sentiment results.

## Change
Provide the two reconstruction arguments through `__getnewargs__`. Assessment metadata continues to use the normal instance-state serialization, including deep-copy isolation. This is scoped to `Score`; it does not change the separate namedtuple types returned by analyzer wrappers.

## Validation
- The 14 new tests on unchanged upstream: 10 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 18 passed, 1 deselected.
- Actual bundled-lexicon results round-trip through pickle protocols 0 through 5, including unknown text with empty assessments. Both copy modes preserve scores and assessments; deep-copy mutation does not affect the original.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Honor sentiment lexicon confidence thresholds
entries.head: c73aad99b611107df739a038bc353d68d57eee92
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`Sentiment` accepts a `confidence` threshold, and its XML loader already checks that threshold before aggregating word senses. The constructor always stores `None`, so the supplied threshold is discarded and low-confidence senses still influence polarity and subjectivity.

## Change
Store the supplied threshold in the existing `_confidence` field. The existing inclusive comparison and default behavior are unchanged. Add XML-backed tests for sense aggregation, synset scores, semantic labels, lazy loading and explicit loading.

## Validation
- The six new tests on unchanged upstream: 5 failed, 1 passed.
- New tests plus all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 10 passed, 1 deselected.
- A controlled lexicon changes `bright` from the unfiltered polarity -0.1 to the high-confidence polarity +0.6; thresholds `None`, 0, 0.5, 0.8 and 1 exercise default, inclusive and fully filtered cases.
- Native package imports, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Reuse lexical sentiment results when returning assessments
entries.head: d1d57c3d39b4733a8ccfbdc59517e45cb6521544
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`PatternAnalyzer.analyze(..., keep_assessments=True)` evaluates the same text twice: once to retrieve assessments and again to retrieve polarity/subjectivity. Both are already available in the first returned `Score`, so every request for assessments repeats tokenization and lexical analysis.

## Change
Retain that `Score` and reuse its assessments and two numeric values. Return fields and namedtuple construction remain unchanged.

## Validation
- The eight new tests on unchanged upstream: 4 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 12 passed, 1 deselected.
- A counting wrapper still invokes the real lexical analyzer and checks identical scores/assessments for both output modes, including empty and Unicode text.
- Warm-cache local timing for an 1,830-character text, 40 calls per repeat and five repeats: median 0.046352775 s before, 0.023087732 s after (about 2.01x for this workload and path). This is a local microbenchmark, not a general throughput guarantee.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Normalize pretokenized sentiment words consistently with text
entries.head: e826598fa26b2ffb0f69a9363c2524799f720b44
entries.published_body:
## Problem
The lexical sentiment engine lowercases string input before lookup, but skips that normalization for a list of tokens. Equivalent pretokenized text can therefore lose known sentiment words, negation, degree modifiers and case-sensitive emoticons. For example, `['GOOD']` scores as neutral while `'GOOD'` has positive polarity.

## Change
Apply the same lowercase normalization to ordered token-list input before assessing it. Dictionary/term weighting and punctuation rules are unchanged.

## Validation
- The nine new tests on unchanged upstream: 7 failed, 2 passed.
- New tests plus all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 13 passed, 1 deselected.
- Actual bundled-English results are compared with equivalent string input, including negation, modifiers, emoticons, lowercase and empty controls. A hand-defined accented Unicode lexicon verifies non-ASCII normalization.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.

entries.title: Resolve known sentiment synset identifiers safely
entries.head: 445080cf5d4910420e8ec5eb8199c21a963a6d2f
entries.published_body:
## Problem
The lexical sentiment engine documents synset-identifier string input, but its identifier branch requires strings to have object-only attributes such as `synonyms`. Known identifiers in the loaded lexicon therefore fall through to ordinary word tokenization and return neutral scores instead of their stored sentiment.

## Change
Resolve a matching identifier only when it actually exists in the lexicon's synset mapping, loading that mapping on first use. Unknown identifier-shaped strings continue through ordinary text assessment. The separate Synset-object path is unchanged.

## Prior fix compatibility
PR #179 and its source change were inspected. That fix prevented arbitrary strings such as `c-17` from raising `AttributeError` by treating them as objects. This change preserves that protection and adds the previously unavailable lookup for known string identifiers. It never reads Synset-object attributes from a plain string.

## Validation
- The nine new tests on unchanged upstream: 5 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus all existing non-slow sentiment tests: 13 passed, 1 deselected.
- XML-backed first-use tests cover adjective, noun, verb, adverb and Cornetto-style IDs. Unknown `c-17`, unknown WordNet-shaped IDs and ordinary text remain controls.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review checked the earlier PR #179 patch and found no overlap or semantic blockers.

entries.title: Accept token sequences in labeled basic-extractor input
entries.head: e7c52c88f04db44259d2c593d542fc5a01ed24d4
entries.published_body:
## Problem
`basic_extractor` rejects labeled training rows when their document is already tokenized: an assertion requires the first document to be a string, although the underlying dataset-to-vocabulary helper supports token iterables. This also rejects an empty first tokenized document.

## Change
Allow labeled rows to reach the existing string-or-token-sequence handling. Invalid noniterable documents still raise the existing malformed-training-data `ValueError`. Bare vocabulary inputs keep their existing path.

## Validation
- The 11 new tests on unchanged upstream: 7 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus existing format and utility tests: 28 passed.
- Hand-written expected feature dictionaries cover list/tuple/iterator documents, list/iterator rows, an empty first document, bare vocabularies and malformed inputs.
- Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review found no blockers.
- The earlier vocabulary-cache change in PR #136 was inspected; it does not fix this string-only validation.

entries.title: fix(metrics): preserve caller-owned detection predictions
entries.head: 7319c06716ee6eb649a8df1069af8044fad9a753
entries.published_body: ## Summary Detection matching clips predicted boxes in place. On CPU the processor can share the caller's tensor storage, so evaluating one document changes the model predictions supplied by the caller. Reusing the same prediction tensor for a larger page then evaluates previously clipped coordinates and can turn a perfect match into a miss. Clip a local copy of the four box-coordinate columns and use that copy for matching. Scores, classes, caller-owned tensors and their backing storage are preserved. The clipping and matching calculations are otherwise unchanged. ## Validation - Added 11 native detection-evaluation cases: the unchanged base has 6 failures and 5 passes; all 11 pass after the fix. - Covers float32/float64 predictions, contiguous and strided tensors, shared backing storage, out-of-bounds and in-bounds boxes, reuse across both page-size orders, unchanged targets, and pages without targets. - Hand-calculated perfect-match metrics verify that local clipping still affects matching correctly. - Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The full optional-dependency suite and GPU execution were not run. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests for input preservation and repeated evaluation. - [x] Preserved matching and score semantics. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: fix(metrics): separate threshold precision from the AP envelope
entries.head: f944cc34a3db5e1409ca2773162c0cb92df9a79d
entries.published_body: ## Summary Fixed-confidence detection precision currently uses the interpolated precision envelope intended for average precision. This lets correct predictions below the selected score threshold inflate the reported precision and F1 for detections above it. For example, with a high-confidence false positive followed by true positives at scores 0.8 and 0.05, threshold 0.1 accepts one true positive and one false positive. Precision should be 1/2, but the AP envelope makes it 2/3. Compute fixed-threshold precision from the actual cumulative TP/FP counts, then construct the interpolated envelope only for AP. Recall, detection matching and AP remain unchanged. ## Validation - Added 13 native `get_metrics` cases: 7 fail and 6 pass on the unchanged base; all 13 pass with this fix. - Hand-calculated precision, recall, F1 and AP cover six thresholds, exact-score boundaries, two input orderings and two-class macro averaging. - The AP checks remain identical at every confidence threshold. - Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The full optional-dependency suite was not run. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests for corrected precision/F1 and unchanged AP. - [x] Kept detection matching and IoU thresholds unchanged. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: fix(lang): treat an empty language selection as automatic
entries.head: dde618b7cefa882017ea5b2778d4f5b5f5da89ed
entries.published_body: ## Summary Passing `languages=[]` to language detection or metadata application raises `IndexError` at `languages[0]`, before either empty-text handling or automatic detection can run. An empty selection is already treated as a default by `check_language_args` and by the later automatic-detection branch. Normalize an empty language list to the existing automatic mode, just like `None`. This also uses the normal short-ASCII fallback. Explicit languages, the empty-string skip sentinel, and validation of non-list inputs retain their existing behavior. ## Validation - Added 18 native cases: 11 fail and 7 pass on the unchanged base. - New and existing language tests: **83 passed, 4 skipped**. The skips are optional backend tests in the existing suite. - Covers actual langdetect output for English/French/Korean, empty/whitespace text, short-text fallback, list/iterator metadata application in whole-document and per-element modes, unchanged input lists, and existing explicit/invalid language options. - Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The full project test suite was not run. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests and documented empty-list behavior. - [x] Preserved explicit language selection and invalid-input checks. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: fix(staging): associate COCO annotations with their source images
entries.head: ff6628b14d12f8406c8aa80e2da07a30e1dda493
entries.published_body: ## Summary Include the matching `image_id` on every annotation produced by `convert_to_coco()`. The current export omits this required relationship, so the native COCO reader raises `KeyError: 'image_id'` while building its index and cannot retrieve training annotations by image. Reuse the existing five image identity fields and preserve their first-seen numbering and deduplication. Multiple elements from the same page share its image ID; different files, directories, pages, or dimensions retain distinct images. Source elements are unchanged. ## Validation - Added 10 regression cases: the unchanged upstream code produces 9 failures and 1 pass; the fix passes all 10. - Exercised a real `pycocotools` 2.0.11 JSON-file load, image indexing, and per-image annotation filtering, alongside repeated pages, all five identity fields, generator input, missing metadata, and empty input. - New tests plus the existing COCO export and coordinate-system module: **27 passed** on Python 3.12. The full repository suite was not run. - Lockfile-pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` passed. ## Checklist - [x] The PR title is a user-facing release-note entry with a conventional commit prefix. - [ ] Please apply the `bug` category label during maintainer triage. - [x] No breaking change, changelog edit, or version bump.

entries.title: fix(metrics): retain detection tensor columns for empty pages
entries.head: 1f5a8a26f6cb57188c503091e504277237c25485
entries.published_body: ## Summary The JSON detection loader converts an empty page to a tensor with shape `(0,)`. Matching expects a prediction matrix with six columns and a target matrix with five columns, so blank pages or pages without annotations raise an `IndexError` during document evaluation. Reshape each loaded page to its declared matrix format. Nonempty page values and layout are unchanged; empty predictions and empty targets can now participate in the existing matching and metric calculations. ## Validation - Added 10 native JSON-to-metrics tests: 7 fail and 3 pass on the unchanged base; all 10 pass after the fix. - Covers all empty/nonempty prediction and target combinations, blank pages at different document positions, false-positive and false-negative pages with hand-calculated precision/recall/F1/AP, and the existing empty-document sentinel. - Preserves the existing undefined (`NaN`) metrics when no class has any ground-truth targets. - Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` pass. The full optional-dependency suite was not run. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests for the behavior change. - [x] Preserved nonempty tensor layout and metric conventions. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: fix(staging): declare Weaviate array metadata as array properties
entries.head: eeae70f9b5c3445a8462a0f9383eb549fe07e22b
entries.published_body: ## Summary Preserve primitive list types when generating a Weaviate collection schema. `stage_for_weaviate()` emits lists for languages, links, email recipients, and emphasized text, but `create_unstructured_weaviate_class()` currently declares these properties as scalar `text` or `int`. The generated schema therefore disagrees with the staged values. Unwrap `Optional` and recognize `list`/`List` annotations for supported primitive types, producing the documented `text[]`, `int[]`, `number[]`, or `date[]` property type. Existing scalar and excluded-field behavior is preserved. ## Validation - Added 22 cases; unchanged upstream produces 19 failures and 3 passes. - Native schema generation and staging cover all ten current primitive-list metadata fields, three scalar controls, and bare/optional/legacy `List` annotation forms. - New and existing Weaviate staging tests: **23 passed, 1 skipped**. The existing database integration test retains its environment-based skip; no Weaviate server upload was run. - Checked the array representation against the [official property data types reference](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/datatypes). - Lockfile-pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` passed. ## Release note This corrects newly generated schemas. Existing collections retain their stored property types and are not migrated by this helper. ## Checklist - [x] The PR title is a user-facing release-note entry with a conventional commit prefix. - [ ] Please apply the `bug` category label during maintainer triage. - [x] No changelog edit or version bump.

entries.title: fix(staging): export COCO boxes in screen coordinates
entries.head: 3f291cdc28bfc14f14298147c0af4a29b9f4eecb
entries.published_body: ## Summary Compute COCO bounding boxes from the bounds of all source vertices in screen coordinates. The current exporter assumes a particular ordering of the first three points and treats every coordinate system as having a top-left origin. This can move a valid rectangle, give a zero height to clockwise vertices, or export Cartesian coordinates on the wrong side of the page. Use the existing coordinate-system conversion to a `PixelSpace` of the same dimensions, then calculate the minimum corner, width, and height. Reuse those dimensions for the existing bounding-box area. Missing coordinates retain their empty-box/`None`-area representation, and source metadata is unchanged. ## Validation - Added 13 regression cases; unchanged upstream produces 11 failures and 2 passes. - Cover four vertex orders in PixelSpace and PointSpace, triangle and diamond bounds, opposite corners, missing coordinates, and source metadata preservation. - A native `pycocotools.mask.iou` calculation confirms unit overlap with the independently specified screen-space rectangle. - New tests plus the existing COCO export and coordinate-system module: **30 passed** on Python 3.12. The full repository suite was not run. - Lockfile-pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` passed. ## Checklist - [x] The PR title is a user-facing release-note entry with a conventional commit prefix. - [ ] Please apply the `bug` category label during maintainer triage. - [x] No changelog edit or version bump; this restores the COCO bounding-box convention.

entries.title: fix(staging): preserve link lists in typed DataFrame exports
entries.head: 50af03296761306f84a19b213054bdf341416860
entries.published_body: ## Summary Keep `link_urls` as an object column when `convert_to_dataframe(..., set_dtypes=True)` applies its dtype map. `ElementMetadata.link_urls` contains a list of strings, but its map entry currently uses `StringDtype`, turning the whole list into a string representation. This loses the sequence structure in JSON records and Hugging Face datasets and prevents URLs from being exploded alongside the corresponding link text and offsets. Use the same object representation already used for other list-valued metadata such as `link_texts`. ## Validation - Added 11 regression cases: unchanged upstream produces 6 failures and 5 passes. - Exercised native pandas multi-column `explode`, JSON records, and `datasets.Dataset.from_pandas`, with typed/untyped controls, missing links, Unicode URLs, and source-metadata preservation. - New tests plus existing DataFrame, pandas-dtype, and flattening tests: **31 passed** on Python 3.12; 65 unrelated tests were deselected. The existing email-derived DataFrame test also passed after its real fixture and dependencies were made available. - Lockfile-pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` passed. The full repository suite was not run. ## Checklist - [x] The PR title is a user-facing release-note entry with a conventional commit prefix. - [ ] Please apply the `bug` category label during maintainer triage. - [x] No changelog edit or version bump.

entries.title: fix(metrics): align detection files by page number
entries.head: d2c1e6121c242bea0306a3cd1ba2f46f7869f1a2
entries.published_body: ## Summary `ObjectDetectionEvalProcessor.from_json_files` validates prediction and ground-truth pages in page-number order, but then constructs tensors and image dimensions using their original JSON order. Two valid files containing the same pages in different orders therefore compare boxes from different pages and report incorrect detection metrics. Sort both freshly loaded page lists once before validation and reuse that ordering for tensor conversion and image dimensions. Input files are unchanged. ## Validation - Added 11 native JSON-to-metrics regression cases. On the unchanged base, 6 fail and 5 pass; all 11 pass with this fix. - Covers independent prediction/target permutations across three pages with distinct sizes and boxes, single-page behavior, page-number mismatch validation, and unchanged input-file contents. - Pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check and format checks and `git diff --check` pass. - The full optional-dependency test suite was not run. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests for the behavior change. - [x] Kept this change limited to detection page alignment. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: fix(sorting): retain positive extents when shrinking thin boxes
entries.head: c35f0f9d96997344393c677da0b4063b00b5afcb
entries.published_body: ## Summary With the default shrink factor, a valid one-pixel-wide or one-pixel-high box is truncated to zero width or height. XY-cut then has no projection for that box and can omit its text element from the sorted page. Fractional page coordinates can also lose their positive extents if they are converted to integers before shrinking. Preserve the original coordinates until shrinking, then keep each strictly positive scaled dimension at least one pixel wide/high on the integer projection grid. The top-left anchor, normal-size integer boxes, originally zero dimensions and an explicit zero shrink factor retain their existing behavior. ## Release note Recovering previously omitted text can change reading order and sequence-derived element IDs. Consumers that persist IDs or compare ordered outputs should account for this corrected output. ## Validation - Added public `sort_page_elements` coverage for fractional narrow width, narrow height and both dimensions, plus originally zero-width/height controls, in both XY-cut directions. The expanded regression file gives **6 failed, 32 passed** before the fractional-coordinate fix and **38 passed** after it. - The complete thin-box regression, sorting and XY-cut test modules pass: **63 passed**. They check returned text, element identity, unchanged input coordinates, integer and fractional boxes, and zero-factor controls. - Verified with Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.4.4, Numba 0.65.0, pytest 9.0.3, unstructured-inference 1.6.12 and OpenCV 4.13.0.92. - Ruff 0.15.10 lint/format and `git diff --check` pass. - Merged main `0bf5f787`; the version guard passes with the unchanged `0.27.38-dev` version. - The full project suite and partition benchmark were not run locally. [Upstream repository CI](https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/actions/runs/43351665781) has now passed on `c35f0f9`. CodeQL and Security still require maintainer approval. [Partition Benchmark](https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/actions/runs/43351665965/job/131653371162) stops before measurement because the Tesseract PPA has no Ubuntu 26.04 `resolute` Release file; the [current main benchmark](https://github.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/actions/runs/43352412529/job/131647266676) fails at the same installation step. ## Checklist - [x] Added regression tests for retained text and unchanged sorting inputs. - [x] Preserved the existing zero-size/zero-factor behavior. - [ ] Apply the `bug` label.

entries.title: [Bugfix] Reject nonpositive offline beam concurrency limits
entries.head: b7b7946da1ef215beb159cd1dd5434ea3018b80a
entries.published_body:
## Problem

A nonpositive `concurrency_limit` in offline beam search is used directly as a `range` step. Zero fails with an incidental range error; negative values skip the generation loop and can return the original prompts as if they were completed beams, with unchanged zero cumulative log probabilities.

## Change

Validate that an explicitly supplied concurrency limit is positive before preprocessing or starting generation. Document the constraint and retain the existing rejection of empty prompt lists.

## Validation

Exact production head: `b7b7946da1ef215beb159cd1dd5434ea3018b80a`.

- 26 new tests run a locally saved tiny GPT-2 through the actual source-built vLLM CPU engine.
- Six nonpositive-limit cases fail on the original source. The other 20 controls pass, including the existing empty-input error contract.
- All 26 cases pass with the patch.
- Valid limits `None`, `1`, `2`, and `8` produce the same tokens, decoded text, and cumulative log probabilities as individual generation for three prompts, using both text and token inputs.
- All 64 existing online beam tests pass.
- The complete applicable repository pre-commit hooks pass.

Native CPU validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43405165739
Repository hooks: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43404085655

The native run uses PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu, verifies exact production source files, and reuses native extensions from the unchanged C++/Rust base.

entries.title: [Bugfix] Honor EOS inclusion consistently in beam-search outputs
entries.head: 17743dbff5b96c393f297a2ce0bc086f72680f22
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Offline beam search always retains a terminating EOS in returned token IDs, regardless of `include_stop_str_in_output`, and does not record its stop metadata. Online beam search already applies the inclusion flag when building completed candidates, but removes a final EOS again when decoding text. Consequently, requesting an included EOS can return token IDs and text that disagree.

## Change

- Record the EOS stop reason for completed offline beams.
- Apply the offline inclusion flag after ranking, before decoding returned tokens.
- Decode online text from the token IDs already selected by the inclusion flag.
- Document the flag's token/text behavior and explicitly retain EOS in the Hugging Face comparison helper.

Beam scores and length penalties continue to use the original log-probability history, including EOS. `ignore_eos=True` continues to treat EOS as an ordinary generated token; `skip_special_tokens` independently controls text decoding.

## Validation

Exact production head: `17743dbff5b96c393f297a2ce0bc086f72680f22`.

- 12 new native tests exercise 32 combinations of special and ordinary generation-config EOS tokens, inclusion, special-token decoding, and ignored EOS.
- A locally saved tiny GPT-2 model runs through the actual offline engine and an actual OpenAI-compatible HTTP server, using source-built vLLM CPU extensions with PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu.
- Original source: 7 failures and 5 passes. Patched source: all 12 pass; all 64 existing online beam-search unit tests also pass.
- Tests check returned token IDs and decoded text, stop metadata, and retained cumulative EOS log probabilities.
- Full repository pre-commit checks pass, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, documentation checks, and test-area coverage. The existing sampler Buildkite area includes the additional dependencies.

Native execution: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43310356124
Full pre-commit: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43308913489

The native execution reuses CPU extensions built from the unchanged C++/Rust base and verifies the exact changed Python files. GPU execution was not part of this validation.

entries.title: [Bugfix] Preserve stable candidate ordering for online beam ties
entries.head: cbffffcca072ed912a38981f0c5571e46804548e
entries.published_body:
## Problem

Online beam search selects active candidates with `argpartition` and an unstable sort. When multiple candidates have the same cumulative score at the beam cutoff, this can retain a different candidate or reorder equal-scoring candidates compared with the stable ordering used by offline beam search.

## Change

Keep partial selection, but determine the cutoff score first, retain all strictly better candidates, and fill the remaining slots with tied candidates in their original order. Stable sorting is then limited to the selected candidates. The small-candidate path also uses stable sorting.

## Validation

Exact production head: `cbffffcca072ed912a38981f0c5571e46804548e`.

- 24 async cases compare the actual online selection path with the actual offline beam step across four beam widths, one/three generation steps, flat distributions, cutoff ties, and distinct token scores that produce cumulative ties.
- The original source fails one regression case; the patched source passes all 24.
- An additional native test runs a locally saved zero-weight GPT-2 through both the offline engine and an actual OpenAI-compatible HTTP server for six beam-width/length configurations. This is a passing compatibility control on both versions.
- All 64 existing online beam tests pass.
- All applicable repository pre-commit hooks pass.

Native CPU validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43405764771
Repository hooks: https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43405770814

The native test uses PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu and source-built CPU extensions from the unchanged native base.

entries.title: [Perf][Pooling] Bound reference MaxSim matrices for long inference pairs
entries.head: 11c0abf92f2b6237cb731050b9617c58da79f4c8
entries.published_body:
## Overview

Keep the reference MaxSim similarity matrix within its element budget during inference, including when a single query/document pair is larger than the entire budget.

## Claims

- Tile oversized single pairs along query and document tokens while preserving FP32 MaxSim scores.
- Keep each temporary similarity matrix within `max_score_matrix_elements`.
- Preserve the existing full-matrix path when input gradients are tracked.

## Validation

- [Native CPU tests and benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43417368801): **2 allocation failures / 20 passes on the original source**, then **22 passes with the change**.
- **9 existing reference-runner tests pass; 2 existing CUDA-only cases are skipped on the CPU host.**
- [Repository pre-commit hooks and Ruff](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43417250570) pass.
- Regression cases cover FP16/BF16/FP32 inputs, strided tensors, different budgets, negative scores, input ownership, allocation bounds, and the unchanged gradient-tracked path.
- A real saved tiny ColBERT model exercises the worker-side scoring path with an 8,193-token query and document. Its score agrees with independently obtained token embeddings.

On an AMD EPYC 7763 CPU host, two Torch threads, three fresh processes per configuration, and seven timed calls per process:

| Query × document tokens | Budget | Original median | Patched median | Original additional peak RSS | Patched additional peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 × 512 | 1,048,576 elements | 0.07358 ms | 0.07326 ms | 5.574 MiB | 5.574 MiB |
| 4,096 × 8,192 | 1,048,576 elements | 48.814 ms | 9.160 ms | 134.008 MiB | 9.684 MiB |

The benchmark uses 16-dimensional embeddings and produces identical scalar scores. These are local reference-scorer measurements, not full-model or GPU throughput claims. The native validation branch contains the benchmark script and per-process results.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_late_interaction_runner.py
pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py -k long_pair_worker
```

## Details

Reducing the number of pairs in a batch cannot shrink the matrix once only one pair remains. The new inference fallback computes document maxima across bounded tiles, concatenates the per-query maxima, and sums them. Ordinary pairs retain the existing batched implementation.

The budget covers the temporary similarity matrix, not model weights, token embeddings, attention memory, or the fused GPU implementation. Gradient-tracked calls keep the original path; this change does not repair the existing backward limitation caused by the original in-place masking.

The final signed commit has exactly the same Git tree as validated commit `ebdd3f7a92c51731a07adc5a3e90a5af6e0ba3b4`; only commit history and the sign-off changed.

entries.title: [Bugfix][Model] Initialize configured ColBERT projections after module setup
entries.head: c04161eda9e574dc5d5b6d0182bbba661830bf21
entries.published_body:
## Overview

Fix loading ColBERT checkpoints that declare their projection width through `colbert_dim`, `dim`, or `projection_dim`.

## Claims

- Construct the projection after `nn.Module` initialization and before the token pooler consumes it.
- Accept both existing projection checkpoint names, `linear.weight` and `colbert_linear.weight`, with configured or inferred dimensions.
- Record both registered names of the shared projection after its weight is actually loaded.

## Validation

- [Native CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43415980870): the same eight new saved-checkpoint cases produce **6 failures / 2 passes on the original source**, then **8 passes with this change**.
- **76 existing pooler head and activation tests pass.**
- [Repository pre-commit hooks and Ruff](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43412052619) pass.
- Each new case saves a local one-layer BERT plus a non-square projection, loads it through the public `LLM` API, and compares token embeddings and MaxSim scores with the actual Transformers encoder and an independent projection reference.
- Validation used the compiled C++/Rust CPU runtime for base `191e5d5`, with PyTorch 2.14. No GPU or distributed-model validation is claimed.

Reproduce the new tests with:

```bash
pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py -k configured_projection
```

## Details

The child constructor initialized the ColBERT projection before the parent initialized `nn.Module`. With an explicit projection dimension, assigning the `Linear` submodule therefore raised `AttributeError` during model startup. Moving that initialization into the existing model-building hook preserves the parent initialization order and makes the projection available to the pooler.

The projection is also registered through the pooler. Its successful checkpoint load now reports both aliases, so the loaded-parameter check agrees with the actual shared module. The inference-dimension path remains covered.

The final signed commit has exactly the same Git tree as validated commit `edb858436acebd612073a859cfd3ea6bb5cf2a48`; only commit history and the sign-off changed.

entries.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Preserve token logprobs under large shared logit offsets
entries.head: a1d104587bcf4b86592fe988ac05f4b6cd47ede4
entries.published_body:
## Overview

Prevent cancellation from corrupting token log probabilities in the standalone CPU model runner when logits share a large offset.

## Claims

- Subtract the row maximum before computing both the selected logit and normalization term.
- Preserve the existing FP32 output and nonfinite-row behavior.
- Keep top-k and prompt-score callers on the same corrected token-logprob implementation.

## Validation

- [Exact-source native ARM CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43419952030): **19 failures / 9 passes on the original source**, then **28 passes with this change**.
- **10 existing CPU logprob tests pass.**
- [Repository pre-commit hooks and Ruff](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43414866395) pass.
- Tests cover FP16/BF16/FP32 logits, positive and negative common offsets, masked and nonfinite rows, empty selected-token sets, top-k scores, and prompt scores.
- Six saved tiny GPT-2 cases exercise the real public `LLM.generate` path in raw and processed logprob modes. The native C++ and Rust runtime was built for the unchanged base `191e5d5` on ARM and reused for the exact final-source run.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/cpu/test_cpu_logprob.py
```

## Details

Computing a large log-normalizer and then subtracting it from a similarly large selected logit discards the small log probability. For example, a real saved tiny GPT-2 with sixteen equal logits of `1e8` returned `0` for each token instead of `-log(16)` (approximately `-2.7725887`). The same failure occurs with a large negative common offset.

The new calculation keeps the common offset out of both terms. This change targets `vllm/v1/worker/cpu/logprob.py`, used by the standalone CPU runner. The x86 Triton runner uses a different implementation; the new end-to-end tests therefore run on native ARM CPU hardware. No GPU path or model-quality improvement is claimed.

The final signed commit has exactly the same Git tree as validated commit `8b376970f56d33e8a543ee90fa69978cffe0d5d0`; only commit history and the sign-off changed.

entries.title: [Bugfix] Preserve lanes when packing narrow integer quantized weights
entries.head: 2e7c853b3b6af28d8fb66923b71a67c74d08d84a
entries.published_body:
## Purpose

`pack_quantized_values_into_int32` shifts each lane while it still has the input tensor's dtype. For int8, uint8, and int16 inputs, bits are truncated (or sign-extended) before the final int32 conversion. This silently corrupts the packed weight words.

## Changes

- Promote int8, uint8, and int16 inputs to int32 before masking and shifting.
- Keep the existing int32 and int64 paths.
- Add 40 independent NumPy uint32 oracle cases covering 4-bit and 8-bit values, both packing dimensions, contiguous and transposed inputs, all five input dtypes, unpacking, and source preservation.

## Validation

[Native CPU before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/vllm/actions/runs/43418160015), using official PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu and source-built vLLM CPU extensions on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C runner:

- Baseline: 33 failures and 18 passes. Fixed: all 51 cases pass, with no errors or skips.
- Those 51 cases include the 40 production packing tests, 8 real FP16/BF16 linear comparisons, and 3 full vLLM Llama inference comparisons.
- For each full Llama comparison, actual pack/unpack output is dequantized and saved as an FP32 checkpoint; inference is compared with an independently dequantized reference checkpoint. Generated tokens match and all checked log probabilities agree within 1e-6.
- One existing CPU WNA16 regression control also passes.
- Ruff check, Ruff format, and diff whitespace checks pass.

The full-model checks exercise checkpoints produced by the packing helper. They use ordinary FP32 inference; they do not exercise a GPTQ/WNA16-quantized model end to end.

Validated source commit: `8b997c34e40ac86091eec2587b2d227ed41bed04`. The submitted signed commit `2e7c853b3b6af28d8fb66923b71a67c74d08d84a` has the identical Git tree `28f35334e025490ec20b0465a5d0707b0e061770`.

Related changes checked: #46136 converts a Humming input to int32 at its call site; #31431 replaces the packing-width constant. Neither fixes narrow inputs to this shared helper.

entries.title: Avoid quadratic traversal in maximum-layer scanning
entries.head: be20c6e91fa30f31b7546a163e5ff7e2f8e119fd
entries.published_body:
## Problem

The maximum-layer scan repeatedly removes the first item of a Python list and prepends each module's children to the remaining list. A wide model hierarchy therefore spends quadratic time moving list entries during device-map planning.

## Change

Use a reversed stack and append children in reverse order. The scan keeps the same depth-first order, maximum layer size, equal-size name ordering, and no-split behavior. This changes only traversal bookkeeping; layer selection and memory accounting remain unchanged.

## Validation

Exact source: `be20c6e91fa30f31b7546a163e5ff7e2f8e119fd`, based on `f5cc53877677eb7fa0ef7091fe41536a777fee6a`.

[Native before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/accelerate/actions/runs/43421469673), Python 3.12 and official PyTorch 2.9.0+cpu:

- The identical final tests pass on both sources: **79 passed, 10 skipped, 4 subtests passed**. This includes 41 new cases and the complete existing `test_modeling_utils.py` group. The skips are the existing hardware/slow-test gates.
- New controls cover CPU/meta modules, FP32/FP64 sizes, reversed input order, no-split classes, equal maxima, zero sizes, tensor leaves, and input-list preservation.
- Eight integration cases train a real model with SGD momentum, save weights and optimizer state, infer the device map for a fresh meta-initialized model, load it with `load_checkpoint_and_dispatch`, and compare two continuation steps' outputs, gradients, parameters, and momentum buffers.
- Ruff 0.13.1 lint/format and whitespace checks pass.

## Measured planning cost

Five timed calls per case on one CPU thread; the benchmark constructs a real `ModuleList` of independent meta `Linear(2, 2)` modules. Construction and precomputed sizes are outside the helper timing. The device-map timing calls the complete `infer_auto_device_map` function, including its size computation. Returned layer names and device maps have identical hashes.

| Leaf modules | Maximum-layer scan before / after | Complete device map before / after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 0.0792 / 0.0793 ms | 0.7132 / 0.7678 ms |
| 8,192 | 17.4639 / 13.0148 ms | 95.1010 / 94.3681 ms |
| 65,536 | 450.5455 / 111.0378 ms | 1121.1533 / 797.0523 ms |

At 65,536 leaves the helper is about **4.06x** faster and complete planning about **1.41x** faster. The helper's measured Python allocation peak decreases from 12,451,762 to 11,928,122 bytes; the complete planner's peak is unchanged at 27,635,863 bytes. Small cases show little benefit and the 64-leaf complete-planning measurement is slightly slower. These are model-planning measurements, not training-throughput or GPU-memory results.

The benchmark and raw results are retained in the separate validation branch/run artifacts; no workflow is added to this PR.

## Before submitting

- [x] Read contributor guidance and checked related history and all-state PRs.
- [x] Added semantic and checkpoint-continuation controls.
- [x] Ran related existing tests on both sources.

Related performance changes #2756 and #3776 optimize balanced-memory leaf bookkeeping, while #4531 changes which tensors count as layers. This patch keeps the existing layer semantics and removes front-of-list traversal costs.

entries.title: Preserve KL forward values when correcting the gradient
entries.head: 3736b55a69bfc63119c06e838cf67c986c714a81
entries.published_body:
## Problem

With `unbiased_gradient=True`, `compute_approx_kl` promises to keep the chosen estimator's forward value and substitute the corrected reverse-KL gradient. The current expression evaluates `value + grad_surrogate` first. A large but finite surrogate can round away part or all of the clipped forward value before the detached surrogate is subtracted.

For example, current/reference log probabilities of -12000 and -1 produce a finite squared surrogate much larger than the clipped k2 value of 10. The current expression returns a different loss even though the gradient correction is intended to affect only backward. Normalized categorical-policy examples and real GPT2 training reproduce the same error.

## Change

Subtract the surrogate and its detached value before adding the detached estimator value:

```python
return value.detach() + (grad_surrogate - grad_surrogate.detach())
```

For finite surrogates, the parenthesized expression is zero in forward and retains the existing surrogate gradient. Estimator selection, clipping, importance weighting and the default `unbiased_gradient=False` path keep their existing formulas.

## Validation

Exact source `3736b55a69bfc63119c06e838cf67c986c714a81`, based on `26494490bc237f6c3af62dab6117e6bbb0a78dba`.

[Native before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/OpenRLHF/actions/runs/43422359359), Python 3.12.16, official PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu, DeepSpeed 0.19.6 and Transformers 5.15.0:

- Identical 44 new tests on the original implementation: **42 failed, 2 passed**.
- Fixed implementation: **44 passed**.
- Existing repository suite: **203 passed, 2 skipped** on the original implementation; the full suite including the new tests is **247 passed, 2 skipped** after the fix.
- Coverage includes k1/k2/k3, on-policy and off-policy weighting, FP16/BF16/FP32/FP64 input tensors, normalized categorical policies, and preserved NaN/invalid-estimator behavior.
- Twelve real GPT2 training cases cover SGD with momentum and AdamW, FP32/FP64 models and all three estimators. Three updates compare reported losses, every parameter gradient, weights and optimizer state against an independently supplied analytic KL-gradient reference. A disk checkpoint after the first update restores the model and optimizer before the remaining updates.
- Compile checks and the repository's Black, isort and autoflake checks pass.

The new tests execute the complete source utility module with installed native dependencies; they do not replace PyTorch or DeepSpeed. Validation is CPU-only. The numerical guarantee is for finite surrogate values; this change does not define behavior for an infinite surrogate minus itself or alter non-finite inputs.

## Prior work checked

All-state issue/PR searches, the affected file's 39-entry history and every existing non-audit/non-validation fork head were checked. #1309 introduced the corrected-gradient expression, #1101 proposed an earlier gradient variant, and #1335 bounds the separate k3 exponential derivative. None preserves the corrected-gradient forward value by changing this evaluation order.

entries.title: Avoid redundant padding copies for single-sequence batches
entries.head: 3737390e06bb85a36f050358f4813807a12e4713
entries.published_body:
## Problem

`zero_pad_sequences` calls `F.pad` even when a batch contains one sequence. Zero-width padding creates a complete clone, and the following `cat` or `stack` allocates the final batch again. This repeated copy occurs in the default microbatch-size-one SFT collation path.

## Change

For a single input, call the existing final `cat`/`stack` directly. The result still owns independent storage and retains the existing shape, layout and autograd behavior. The condition follows from the batch structure: one input cannot need padding to match another input. Multi-input batches keep the original padding loop.

## Validation

- Independent upstream base: `26494490bc237f6c3af62dab6117e6bbb0a78dba`.
- Native CPU regression file: 78 passes and two allocation-budget failures before; 80 passes after. All original semantic controls pass.
- Covers left/right padding, cat/stack, numeric and Boolean tensors, empty tensors, single/multiple sequences, noncontiguous and expanded views, channels-last layout, output storage independence, exact output strides and gradients.
- Actual `SFTDataset` and `DataLoader` with a local tokenizer feed GPT2 through three SGD updates. Every parameter matches the existing collation algorithm for microbatch sizes 1 and 2 in SFT and pretraining modes.
- `python -m compileall -q openrlhf examples tests` passes; the full `python -m pytest -q` run reports 283 passed and 2 skipped.
- All repository pre-commit hooks pass on the exact source commit, including Black, isort and autoflake.
